definition_zh: 威权的；专制的；要求服从的；威权主义者；家长式的
definition_en: demanding obedience and allowing little freedom, or relating to a system that concentrates power in an authority
core_image: 办公桌后坐着一位上司，桌上立着一块牌写着「照我说的做」，门外的人排队等候批准
scene: 新经理上任后，所有决定都要经他一人签字，员工连改一行文案也要等批准。 The new manager ran an authoritarian office where no one dared to disagree.
sceneCN: 新经理上任后，所有决定都要经他一人签字，员工连改一行文案也要等批准；句中这个词指「要求服从、几乎不容自由的」（第 1 个义项：以权威为中心、限制异议与自主的制度或作风）。句意为新经理把一个办公室管成威权式的，没人敢表示不同意见。可辨识物件：签字笔、审批单、门口排队的人、写有命令的牌子。

pos.zh: 威权的；专制的；要求服从的
家长式的；管得过严的（口语）
威权主义者；主张集中权力的人

senses.title: Demanding obedience
senses.definition: expecting people to comply without question and treating disagreement as a problem
senses.definitionCN: 要求人们无条件服从，并把异议视为问题
senses.example: The new manager ran an authoritarian office where no one dared to disagree.
senses.exampleCN: 新经理把一个办公室管成威权式的，没人敢表示不同意见。
senses.why: The suffix -arian forms an adjective of adherence, so the word describes a way of holding authority rather than an office.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -arian 构成表示信奉的形容词，因此这个词描述握有权威的方式，而非某个职位。

senses.title: Relating to authoritarian government
senses.definition: belonging to a system in which power is concentrated and elections, if held, are not competitive
senses.definitionCN: 属于权力集中、即使有选举也缺乏竞争的体制
senses.example: The regime was authoritarian but kept elections for show.
senses.exampleCN: 这个政权是威权式的，却保留选举作为门面。
senses.why: Political science needed a word for systems that are neither democratic nor fully totalitarian, and this adjective filled the gap.
senses.whyCN: 政治学需要一个词来描述既非民主、也非完全极权的体制，这个形容词填补了空缺。

senses.title: A person who favours such rule
senses.definition: someone who believes order requires concentrated, unchallenged authority
senses.definitionCN: 认为秩序需要集中而不容挑战的权威的人
senses.example: Authoritarians distrust open debate.
senses.exampleCN: 威权主义者不信任公开辩论。
senses.why: One form serves as adjective and person-noun, so the believer and the belief look identical.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形式兼作形容词与指人的名词，因此信徒与信条看起来一样。

senses.title: A parenting style
senses.definition: raising children with strict rules and little room for discussion or autonomy
senses.definitionCN: 以严格规则养育孩子，很少给讨论或自主空间
senses.example: Authoritarian parents set rules without discussion.
senses.exampleCN: 专制型父母立规矩而不讨论。
senses.why: The political word is borrowed for the family, the smallest place where unchecked authority is exercised.
senses.whyCN: 这个政治词被借来描述家庭，也就是行使不受制约权威的最小场所。

senses.title: A management style
senses.definition: running a workplace by centralised approval and one-way instruction
senses.definitionCN: 靠集中审批与单向指令运行工作场所
senses.example: An authoritarian boss centralises every approval.
senses.exampleCN: 威权式上司把每一项批准都集中到自己手里。
senses.why: Workplaces reproduce the state in miniature, so the same adjective describes a chain of approvals.
senses.whyCN: 工作场所是国家的缩小复制，因此同一个形容词可描述审批链。

senses.title: A personality trait
senses.definition: a disposition that prefers rigid order, hierarchy and submission to authority
senses.definitionCN: 偏好僵化的秩序、等级与服从权威的性情
senses.example: His authoritarian streak showed in small rules.
senses.exampleCN: 他的威权倾向体现在一条条小规矩里。
senses.why: Twentieth-century psychology turned a political adjective into a measurable trait, which is why questionnaires use the word.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪心理学把这个政治形容词变成可测量的特质，因此问卷会用到这个词。

senses.title: An institutional culture
senses.definition: a habit inside an organization that punishes criticism and rewards deference
senses.definitionCN: 机构内部惩罚批评、奖励顺从的习惯
senses.example: The university's authoritarian culture discouraged criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学的威权文化压制了批评。
senses.why: Culture is authority without a visible ruler, so the word can describe an atmosphere rather than a person.
senses.whyCN: 文化是没有可见统治者的权威，因此这个词可描述氛围，而非某个人。

senses.title: Order valued above liberty
senses.definition: characteristic of an ideology that treats stability and obedience as higher goods than freedom
senses.definitionCN: 把稳定与服从视为高于自由的价值的意识形态特征
senses.example: The party's authoritarian ideology valued order over liberty.
senses.exampleCN: 这个政党的威权意识形态把秩序看得高于自由。
senses.why: The adjective also marks a value ranking, which is the ideological core behind the institutional forms.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也标出一种价值排序，而那正是制度形式背后的意识形态核心。

intro.en: Authoritarian is authority plus the suffix -arian, modelled on French autoritaire. English used it from the nineteenth century for systems that concentrate power, and the twentieth century extended it to personalities and management.
intro.cn: authoritarian 是 authority 加后缀 -arian，仿法语 autoritaire 构成。英语从十九世纪起用它指集中权力的体制，二十世纪又扩展到人格与管理。

items.en: Augere meant 'to increase, to grow'. Its Indo-European source is reconstructed, so the older root is a reconstruction rather than an attested form.
items.cn: augere 意为「增加、生长」。它的印欧来源是重构的，因此更早的词根是重构形式，而非有书证的形式。

items.en: Auctor meant 'originator, promoter, author', the person who makes something grow or brings it about. The word began with creation, not with command.
items.cn: auctor 意为「发起者、推动者、作者」，即使某物生长或促成其事的人。这个词从创造开始，而非从命令开始。

items.en: Auctoritas meant 'advice, influence, prestige, command'. Roman authority rested on recognized standing as much as on force, a nuance the modern adjective tends to flatten.
items.cn: auctoritas 意为「建议、影响、威望、命令」。罗马的权威既靠公认地位，也靠武力，现代形容词往往抹平这一细微差别。

items.en: English authority is recorded from the Middle Ages, first for a right to command and later for an expert source. The noun still carries both readings.
items.cn: 英语 authority 自中世纪起有书证，先指发令的权利，后指专家性来源。这个名词至今兼有这两种读法。

items.en: The suffix -arian marks a person or thing that adheres to a principle, as in egalitarian and vegetarian. Added to authority it names adherence to concentrated authority.
items.cn: 后缀 -arian 标出信奉某一原则的人或事物，如 egalitarian 与 vegetarian。加在 authority 上，它指对集中权威的信奉。

items.en: The adjective fixed as a technical term for non-democratic but not fully totalitarian systems in the twentieth century, and psychology applied it to personalities after 1950. Source uncertain (first date): the earliest technical citation is not fixed.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个形容词固定为指「非民主但未达完全极权」体制的术语；心理学在 1950 年之后把它用于人格。首见年代不确定：最早的技术性书证并无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin auctor root or with a confusingly similar shape; group two holds adjectives for neighbouring kinds of concentrated rule.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁 auctor 词根或外形近似到易混的词；第二组是描述相邻集中统治类型的形容词。

entries.definition: The right or power to command, or an expert body. Authoritarian is the adjective for a way of using that power.
entries.definitionCN: 指发令的权利或权力，或专家机构。authoritarian 是描述使用这种权力方式的形容词。

entries.definition: Trustworthy and expert, as in an authoritative account. It is often confused with authoritarian, but it praises reliability rather than obedience.
entries.definitionCN: 指可信且有专家根据，如权威性的记述。它常与 authoritarian 混淆，但它赞扬可靠性，而非要求服从。

entries.definition: The doctrine or regime; authoritarian is the adjective or the person who supports it.
entries.definitionCN: 指学说或政权；authoritarian 是形容词或支持者。

entries.definition: A person who writes or creates something, from the same Latin root. The word began with making, not with ruling.
entries.definitionCN: 指写作或创造某物的人，同出拉丁词根。这个词始于创造，而非统治。

entries.definition: From Greek authentikos 'original, genuine', not from Latin auctor. It means real or genuine and has no connection with authority.
entries.definitionCN: 出自希腊 authentikos「原本的、真正的」，并非拉丁 auctor。它意为真实、真品，与权威无关。

entries.definition: Relating to rule by one person with sole authority; it stresses the number of rulers, while authoritarian stresses the demand for obedience.
entries.definitionCN: 与一人独掌权威的统治相关；它强调统治者人数，而 authoritarian 强调要求服从。

entries.definition: Like a dictator: unchecked and often arbitrary. Authoritarian can describe a legal system with elections, so it is sometimes softer.
entries.definitionCN: 像独裁者一样：不受制约且往往任意。authoritarian 可描述带选举的法律制度，因此有时语气较缓。

entries.definition: Exercising power at a ruler's whim; the word judges the rule harshly, while authoritarian is a cooler analytical label.
entries.definitionCN: 按统治者心意行使权力；这个词严厉评判统治，而 authoritarian 是较冷静的分析标签。

entries.definition: Seeking control over every part of life, including private thought; it is a stronger claim than authoritarian, which can allow a private sphere.
entries.definitionCN: 试图控制生活的每一部分，包括私人思想；它比 authoritarian 是更强的断言，后者可允许私人领域存在。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin root, a real suffix of adherence and real social-science phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、真实的表信奉后缀与真实的社会科学用语。

normal.en: Authority plus -arian: the ending means adherence, so the word names those who cling to concentrated authority.
normal.cn: authority 加 -arian：词尾意为信奉，因此这个词指紧抓集中权威的人。

normal.en: The family runs authority, authorize, authoritative, authoritarian, authoritarianism.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 authority、authorize、authoritative、authoritarian、authoritarianism。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: an authoritarian regime, authoritarian personality, authoritarian parenting.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：威权政权、威权人格、专制型教养。

normal.en: Do not confuse authoritative with authoritarian: one means reliable, the other means bossy.
normal.cn: 不要把 authoritative 与 authoritarian 混淆：一个意为可信，一个意为专横。

normal.en: The root began with growth and creation, not with command.
normal.cn: 这个词根最初表示生长与创造，而非命令。

abstract.en: Picture a door with a sign that says do as I say, and no handle on your side.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，挂着「照我说的做」的牌子，你这一侧没有门把手。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder where every rung is an approval stamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子，每一级都是一个审批印章。

abstract.en: Picture a room where the thermostat is locked behind glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，恒温器被锁在玻璃后面。

examples.en: The country moved from an authoritarian regime to a fragile democracy.
examples.cn: 这个国家从威权政权走向脆弱的民主。

examples.en: Authoritarian management drove away the most experienced staff.
examples.cn: 威权式管理赶走了最有经验的员工。

examples.en: The study measured authoritarian attitudes among first-year students.
examples.cn: 这项研究测量了一年级学生的威权态度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「权威」加「信奉」：信奉集中权威、要求服从；这属构词说明，并非谐音联想

root: 拉丁 augere「增加、生长」（更早词根为重构形式）→ auctor「发起者、作者」→ auctoritas「建议、影响、命令」→ 英语 authority；加后缀 -arian（信奉……的，仿法语 autoritaire）构成 authoritarian（十九世纪）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a way of holding power to a way of ranking values: obedience demanded, a regime, a believer, a parent, a boss, a personality, a culture and an ideology that prefers order to liberty.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从握权方式走向价值排序：要求服从、政权、信奉者、父母、上司、人格、文化，以及把秩序置于自由之上的意识形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a desk with a sign reading do as I say, a pen for every approval, and a queue waiting outside the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张桌子，牌子上写着「照我说的做」，每份批准都要用那支笔，门外排着等候的人。

branches.en: The demand for obedience and the ranking of order above liberty are one preference seen as habit and as doctrine.
branches.cn: 要求服从与把秩序置于自由之上，是同一偏好在习惯与教义两个层面的呈现。

branches.en: A regime is the demand written into law, with elections kept only as a façade.
branches.cn: 政权是把这一要求写进法律，选举只留作门面。

branches.en: A believer and the belief share one form, which is why the adjective can also name a person.
branches.cn: 信徒与信条共用同一个形式，因此这个形容词也能指人。

branches.en: The family and the university are the same authority at two sizes, one with children and one with colleagues.
branches.cn: 家庭与大学是同一权威的两种尺寸，一个面对孩子，一个面对同事。

branches.en: A boss and a personality are the same trait seen from outside and from inside.
branches.cn: 上司与人格是同一特质从外部与内部看到的两种样子。

intro.en: Authoritarian is a Latin noun of authority plus a suffix of adherence, so it reads as 'one who holds to concentrated authority'.
intro.cn: authoritarian 是表示权威的拉丁名词加表信奉的后缀，因此可读作「信奉集中权威者」。

latinIntro.en: Latin auctor and auctoritas supply the base; auctor comes from augere 'to increase', whose older Indo-European root is reconstructed rather than attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 auctor 与 auctoritas 提供基础；auctor 出自 augere「增加」，其更早的印欧词根是重构的，而非有书证的。

items.example: The root begins with growth, not with command.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根始于生长，而非命令。

items.example: The person-word names one who brings something about.
items.exampleCN: 这个指人的词指促成某事的人。

items.example: The abstract noun adds standing and weight to the person.
items.exampleCN: 抽象名词在个人之上加上了地位与分量。

items.meaning: the right to command; an expert body
items.example: English took the noun in the Middle Ages.
items.exampleCN: 英语在中世纪借入这个名词。

items.example: The suffix marks adherence to a principle.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标出对某一原则的信奉。

items.example: English formed the adjective in the nineteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 英语在十九世纪构成这个形容词。

items.example: A true friend of the word, often mistaken for the other.
items.exampleCN: 这是这个词真正的近亲，却常被误认作另一词。

items.example: The verb names the act of granting authority.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指授予权威的行为。

items.example: The oldest sense is creation, not rule.
items.exampleCN: 最古老的含义是创造，而非统治。

definition_zh: 凹室；壁龛；（花园中的）凉亭
definition_en: a small recessed space in a room, or a sheltered place in a garden
core_image: 墙里挖出的一个小天地：三面有壁，一人一椅刚刚好
scene: 书房一侧的墙凹进去，摆着一张书桌，正好容得下一个人。 He sat reading in the alcove by the window.
sceneCN: 这里 alcove 是「凹室」（第 1 个义项：墙体凹入形成的小空间）；句意是他坐在窗边的凹室里读书。

derivatives.zh: alcove 加 -ed 转作形容词（罕用），义为「带凹室的」
义近的姊妹词，源自法语，义为「壁龛；（喻）定位」

senses.title: A recessed space in a room
senses.definition: a small partly enclosed space formed by part of a wall set back
senses.definitionCN: 由墙面内凹形成、部分围合的小空间
senses.example: The bed fits neatly into an alcove in the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 床正好嵌进墙上的凹室里。
senses.why: The Arabic word named a vaulted or arched recess, and English kept the picture of a space cut into a wall.
senses.whyCN: 阿拉伯语原词指带拱顶的凹处，英语保留了「从墙体里切出一块空间」的画面。

senses.title: A sheltered spot in a garden
senses.definition: a small sheltered area outdoors, often shaded by trees or built as a bower
senses.definitionCN: 户外的遮蔽小境，常由树荫围合或筑成亭阁
senses.example: Vines shaded the garden alcove where they drank their coffee.
senses.exampleCN: 藤蔓给花园凉亭搭起荫凉，他们在那里喝咖啡。
senses.why: A sheltered outdoor nook works like an indoor recess, so the same word covers the bower among the trees.
senses.whyCN: 户外的避风小境功能上如同室内的凹龛，于是同一个词也覆盖了树间的亭阁。

intro.en: From Arabic for 'the vault', travelling through Spanish into English architecture.
intro.cn: 源自阿拉伯语「拱顶」，经西班牙语进入英语建筑词汇。

items.en: al-qubba meant the vault or dome, with the article al- attached.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 al-qubba 意为「拱顶、穹顶」，al- 为定冠词。

items.en: Spanish alcoba kept the sense of a vaulted recess or bedroom alcove.
items.cn: 西班牙语 alcoba 保留「拱形凹室、卧室凹龛」之义。

items.en: French alcôve broadened the word to garden shelters as well.
items.cn: 法语 alcôve 把词义扩及花园凉亭。

items.en: English alcove entered in the 17th century, first for recesses in rooms.
items.cn: 17 世纪英语借入 alcove，最初指室内凹室。

items.en: Today it names any cozy recess, from bedrooms to breakfast nooks.
items.cn: 现代英语泛指一切舒适的凹入空间，从卧室龛到早餐角。

note.en: The first group gathers Arabic al- cousins and a sound-alike; the second gathers words for recessed spaces.
note.cn: 第一组收阿拉伯语 al- 同源词与音近词；第二组收表示「凹入空间」的词。

entries.definition: having an alcove or alcoves
entries.definitionCN: 带凹室的

entries.definition: a chemical substance; shares the Arabic article al-, otherwise unrelated in meaning
entries.definitionCN: 碱；同以阿拉伯语 al- 开头，语义无关

entries.definition: a puckered fabric; only vaguely similar in ending, unrelated root
entries.definitionCN: 纹凸织物；仅词尾略似，词源无关

entries.definition: a small sheltered corner, informal
entries.definitionCN: 小角落；隐蔽处，口语化

entries.definition: a space set back into a wall
entries.definitionCN: 壁凹；墙内凹进的空间

entries.definition: a recess, especially for a statue or ornament
entries.definitionCN: 壁龛；（喻）合适的定位

entries.definition: a shady, leafy shelter in a garden
entries.definitionCN: 树荫凉亭；幽居处，文学用法

entries.definition: a small partitioned space for one person
entries.definitionCN: 小隔间；单人隔开的格子间

normalIntro.en: al- is the Arabic article and -cove suggests a sheltered hollow, like a cove on a coast.
normalIntro.cn: al- 是阿拉伯语冠词，-cove 让人想起海湾的避风小湾：一个被围起来的小天地。

normal.en: al-qubba meant the vault; alcove keeps the arch.
normal.cn: al-qubba 意为拱顶，alcove 保留了拱形。

normal.en: Think of a bed set into the wall: an alcove bed.
normal.cn: 想想嵌进墙里的床：alcove bed。

normal.en: A breakfast alcove is a table tucked into a recess.
normal.cn: 早餐角就是把桌子塞进凹室的布置。

normal.en: Al- words from Arabic: alcove, alcohol, algebra.
normal.cn: 来自阿拉伯语的 al- 词：alcove、alcohol、algebra。

normal.en: Niche and nook are near neighbours of alcove.
normal.cn: niche 与 nook 是 alcove 的近邻词。

abstract.en: Picture a child hiding in a space the wardrobe leaves against the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子躲在衣柜与墙之间的小空间里。

abstract.en: See a lamp, a chair, and one reader inside three walls.
abstract.cn: 想象三面墙里的一盏灯、一把椅、一个读书人。

abstract.en: Imagine vines closing over a bench like green curtains.
abstract.cn: 想象藤蔓像绿帘一样罩住长凳。

examples.en: She carved a tiny alcove for her book collection.
examples.cn: 她为藏书凿出一个小小的壁龛。

examples.en: The apartment's sleeping alcove faces east.
examples.cn: 公寓的睡眠凹室朝东。

examples.en: They whispered together in a shadowy alcove of the hall.
examples.cn: 他们在大厅一个幽暗的凹室里低声交谈。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱靠屋」——爱人靠墙凹进去的小角落，一坐就是一下午。

root: 阿拉伯语 al-qubba「拱顶」（al- 为定冠词）经西班牙语 alcoba、法语 alcôve 于 17 世纪进入英语，由「拱形凹处」泛化为室内凹室与园中凉亭。

definition_zh: 暖锋；暖锋过境；暖锋云系；缓慢升温
definition_en: the leading edge of a warm air mass riding up over colder air, marked by layered cloud and steady rain
core_image: 暖空气沿一道缓坡爬上冷空气，云层像层层台阶铺开，细雨连绵不断
scene: 南来的暖湿空气缓缓爬上来，雨丝连着下了两天。 The warm front brought two days of steady drizzle.
sceneCN: 这里指「暖气团爬升到冷气团之上的前沿」（第 1 个义项：暖空气主导推进的锋面）；句意为暖锋带来了连续两天的细雨。图中可辨识物件：缓坡状的交界面、层层铺开的云、持续的雨丝、上升的温度计。

pos.zh: 暖锋；暖锋过境；暖锋云系

collocations.phrase: the warm front lifted over the cold air

senses.title: The leading edge of advancing warm air
senses.definition: the boundary along which a warmer air mass rides up over a colder one
senses.definitionCN: 较暖气团爬到较冷气团之上的交界面
senses.example: The warm front brought two days of steady drizzle.
senses.exampleCN: 暖锋带来了连续两天的细雨。
senses.why: Warm air is less dense, so it climbs the cold air instead of burrowing under it.
senses.whyCN: 暖空气密度更小，因此顺着冷空气向上爬，而不是钻到它下面。

senses.title: The weather of its passage
senses.definition: the sequence of thickening cloud, steady rain and slowly rising temperature as the front passes
senses.definitionCN: 锋面经过时云层加厚、降雨持续、气温缓慢上升的序列
senses.example: During the warm front passage the rain never quite stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 暖锋过境期间，雨几乎没有停过。
senses.why: Because the ascent is gentle and widespread, rain is steady rather than showery.
senses.whyCN: 由于抬升平缓而范围广，降雨是持续的而非阵性的。

senses.title: The layered sequence of cloud
senses.definition: the ordered cloud types from high cirrus through altostratus to low nimbostratus ahead of the front
senses.definitionCN: 锋前由高云向下依次出现的卷云、高层云与雨层云序列
senses.example: Cirrus first, then altostratus: the warm front announced itself hours ahead.
senses.exampleCN: 先是卷云，再是高层云：暖锋提前数小时就自我宣告了。
senses.why: A shallow slope means the cloud is spread over hundreds of kilometres, so the sequence arrives as a timetable.
senses.whyCN: 坡度平缓意味着云铺展在数百公里上，因此云的序列像时刻表一样依次到达。

senses.title: A gentle slope and a wide rain shield
senses.definition: the shallow incline and broad precipitation area that distinguish a warm front from a cold front
senses.definitionCN: 使暖锋区别于冷锋的平缓坡度与宽阔降水区
senses.example: Its gentle slope spread the rain across three provinces.
senses.exampleCN: 其平缓坡度把降雨铺展到三个省。
senses.why: The same volume of lifted air is spread over a much longer distance, so rain is lighter but wider.
senses.whyCN: 同样体积的抬升空气被摊在更长的距离上，因此雨更轻但范围更广。

senses.title: The semicircle symbol on a chart
senses.definition: the line of filled semicircles on a synoptic chart showing the direction warm air is advancing
senses.definitionCN: 天气图上用实心半圆标示暖空气推进方向的线
senses.example: The map drew the warm front with semicircles pointing north.
senses.exampleCN: 地图用朝北的半圆画出暖锋。
senses.why: The semicircles mark the side toward which the warm air is moving.
senses.whyCN: 半圆标出暖空气正在前往的那一侧。

senses.title: Freezing rain above a cold layer
senses.definition: the condition in which rain falling from a warm layer aloft freezes on contact with cold air or ground below
senses.definitionCN: 高空暖层落下的雨在接触下方冷空气或地面时冻结的情形
senses.example: A warm front aloft produced freezing rain across the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 高空的暖锋在整个山谷造成冻雨。
senses.why: Warm air can sit above cold air, so the front's rain passes through a freezing layer before landing.
senses.whyCN: 暖空气可以停在冷空气之上，因此锋面的雨在落地前要穿过一层冰点以下空气。

senses.title: The warm sector ahead of it
senses.definition: the wedge of warm air between a warm front and the cold front behind it
senses.definitionCN: 暖锋与其后冷锋之间那块暖空气楔形区
senses.example: The warm sector stayed humid and hazy for a day.
senses.exampleCN: 暖区潮湿而朦胧，持续了一天。
senses.why: In a mid-latitude cyclone the warm air occupies a sector, and that sector has its own weather.
senses.whyCN: 在中纬度气旋中，暖空气占据一个扇形区域，该区域有自己的天气。

senses.title: A gradual, mild change, figuratively
senses.definition: a slow, gentle change toward a warmer or friendlier state
senses.definitionCN: 朝更温暖或更友好状态缓慢温和的变化
senses.example: The treaty worked like a warm front on relations between the towns.
senses.exampleCN: 这份条约对两镇关系的作用像一道暖锋。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the gentleness and the gradual warming, not the rain.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻保留温和与渐暖，而不保留降雨。

intro.en: Warm front joins the native adjective warm, from Old English wearm, with front, from Latin frons 'forehead, front'. Meteorology coined the phrase in the early twentieth century for the front led by advancing warm air.
intro.cn: warm front 由本族形容词 warm（古英语 wearm）与 front（拉丁 frons「额头、正面」）组合。气象学在 20 世纪初用这个短语指由暖空气主导推进的锋。

items.en: Wearm is the native word for moderately hot, cognate with German warm and Dutch warm.
items.cn: wearm 是表示温暖的本族词，与德语 warm、荷兰语 warm 同源。

items.en: Front came through French from Latin frons, frontis, naming the forehead and then any forward face or boundary.
items.cn: front 经法语来自拉丁 frons, frontis，指额头，进而指任何朝前的一面或交界。

items.en: Bergen forecasters of the 1910s and 1920s paired warm fronts with cold fronts and gave each its own symbol.
items.cn: 20 世纪一十至二十年代的卑尔根预报员把暖锋与冷锋配对，并各给一个符号。

items.en: The Norwegian cyclone model placed the warm sector between the two fronts, explaining its humid weather.
items.cn: 挪威气旋模型把暖区置于两条锋之间，从而解释了暖区潮湿的天气。

items.en: Twentieth-century aviation forecasts fixed the phrase in routine use, especially for icing and low cloud.
items.cn: 20 世纪的航空预报把这个短语固定于日常使用，尤其用于结冰与低云。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the first printed use is dated differently across histories; the formation of the phrase is not in doubt.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：最早书证在不同史著中年代不一；短语的构成并无疑义。

note.en: Group one holds the sibling front types and the base word; group two holds words for mild air and for the warm wedge itself.
note.cn: 第一组是同类锋型与原词；第二组是表示温和空气与暖空气楔的词。

entries.definition: The general boundary between air masses, without saying which body advances.
entries.definitionCN: 气团间的一般交界，不说明哪一团在推进。

entries.definition: The steep edge of cold air wedging under warm air, with squalls and a sharp drop.
entries.definitionCN: 冷空气楔入暖空气下方的陡峭边缘，伴飑与骤降。

entries.definition: A front that has stopped moving, so rain can persist over one district for days.
entries.definitionCN: 停止移动的锋，因此降雨可在同一地区持续数日。

entries.definition: A period of warmer weather that melts snow and ice; it is the result, not the boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 使冰雪融化的回暖期；是结果，而非交界。

entries.definition: A stretch of unusually mild weather in a cold season; it says nothing about fronts.
entries.definitionCN: 冷季中一段异常温和的天气；不涉及锋面。

entries.definition: The wedge of warm air between a warm front and a following cold front.
entries.definitionCN: 暖锋与其后冷锋之间的暖空气楔形区。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real native warm, the real Latin front and the real layered cloud sequence.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的本族「暖」、真实的拉丁「正面」与真实的层状云序列。

normal.en: Warm air is lighter, so it climbs; cold air is heavier, so it wedges under.
normal.cn: 暖空气更轻，因此向上爬；冷空气更重，因此向下楔入。

normal.en: The cloud arrives as a timetable: cirrus, altostratus, nimbostratus.
normal.cn: 云按时刻表到达：卷云、高层云、雨层云。

normal.en: Gentle slope means light rain over a wide area.
normal.cn: 坡度平缓意味着雨轻而范围广。

normal.en: On a chart, semicircles point the way the warm air is going.
normal.cn: 天气图上，半圆指向暖空气前进的方向。

normal.en: The warm sector sits between the warm front and the cold front behind it.
normal.cn: 暖区位于暖锋与其后的冷锋之间。

abstract.en: Picture a blanket laid gently over a colder floor, warming it slowly.
abstract.cn: 想象一条毯子轻轻盖在更冷的地面上，慢慢把它焐热。

abstract.en: Picture rain that arrives as a schedule rather than a shout.
abstract.cn: 想象一场像日程表而非喊声那样到来的雨。

abstract.en: Picture a friendship that thaws by one degree a day.
abstract.cn: 想象一段友情每天回暖一度。

examples.en: Ahead of the warm front the pressure fell steadily for twelve hours.
examples.cn: 暖锋到来前，气压连续十二小时稳定下降。

examples.en: The warm front lifted over the cold valley air and produced freezing rain.
examples.cn: 暖锋沿冷谷空气爬升，造成了冻雨。

examples.en: After the warm front passed, the snow line retreated up the slope.
examples.cn: 暖锋过境后，雪线沿山坡上退。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「warm（暖）+ front（前沿）」——暖空气推进的前沿 → 暖锋

root: warm 为古英语 wearm「温暖」，与德语 warm、荷兰语 warm 同源；front 经法语出自拉丁 frons, frontis「额头、正面」。短语为 20 世纪初气象学术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the advancing warm edge to its steady rain, layered cloud, gentle slope, chart symbol, freezing rain, warm sector and finally a gradual thaw in relations.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从暖空气推进的边缘，走到持续降雨、层状云、平缓坡度、天气图符号、冻雨、暖区，最后是关系中渐进的回暖。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: warm air climbing a long shallow ramp, laying cloud across the sky like steps.
core.cn: 核心意象：暖空气沿一条长长缓坡向上爬，把云像台阶一样铺满天空。

branches.en: THE RAMP: density decides the climb, and a shallow slope spreads the weather wide.
branches.cn: 缓坡：密度决定爬升，平缓坡度把天气摊得很宽。

branches.en: TIMETABLE: layered cloud and steady rain arrive in a fixed order.
branches.cn: 时刻表：层状云与持续雨按固定顺序到达。

branches.en: SYMBOL: semicircles mark the direction of the warm advance.
branches.cn: 符号：半圆标记暖空气推进的方向。

branches.en: STRUCTURE: warm air can sit aloft over cold air, and the warm sector is its wedge.
branches.cn: 结构：暖空气可以停在冷空气之上，暖区就是它的楔形区。

branches.en: METAPHOR: gentleness and gradual warming survive; rain does not.
branches.cn: 比喻：温和与渐暖留下，降雨被去掉。

intro.en: Warm front is an English noun phrase of a native adjective plus a Latin-derived noun; its technical family uses prefixes and compounds.
intro.cn: warm front 是由本族形容词加拉丁来源名词构成的英语名词短语；其技术词族使用前缀与复合成分。

latinIntro.en: Latin frons supplies front; Latin calidus and tepidus name warmth, though English warm itself is native.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 frons 提供 front；拉丁 calidus 与 tepidus 表示温暖，但英语 warm 本身是本族词。

definition_zh: 繁殖；复制品；再生产；再现；声音还原；翻印
definition_en: the process of producing new individuals or new copies of something already made
core_image: 温室里，一株母株旁边并排长出三株一模一样的小苗，每片叶子的纹路都相同。
scene: 园艺师指着温室里的三株小苗说，它们都是从同一株母本繁殖出来的，叶形和花纹完全一样。 These three seedlings are reproductions of a single parent plant, with exactly the same leaves.
sceneCN: 这里 reproduction 是“生物的繁殖”（第 1 个义项）；句意：这三株小苗由同一母本繁殖而来。

pos.zh: 繁殖；复制；复制品；再生产；再现

senses.title: Making new living things
senses.definition: the biological process by which organisms produce new individuals of their own kind
senses.definitionCN: 生物产生同类新个体的生物学过程
senses.example: Fungi can spread by asexual reproduction alone.
senses.exampleCN: 真菌可以仅靠无性繁殖扩散。
senses.why: The prefix re- means again and production means bringing forth; a species brings forth its kind again, so the same form returns in a new body.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 re- 表示“再一次”，production 表示“产出”；物种把自己的种类再一次产出，同一形制在新个体身上重现。

senses.title: A copy of a work
senses.titleCN: 复制品：仿照原件做出的成品
senses.definition: a copy of a painting, document, or object, often made later and worth less than the original
senses.definitionCN: 对绘画、文件或器物的仿制，通常晚于原件且价值较低
senses.example: The museum displays a reproduction of the tablet, not the original.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆展出的是那块泥板的复制品，而非原件。
senses.why: A copy brings the object forth again in another material; re- marks the second coming, and the copy is openly secondary.
senses.whyCN: 复制品用另一种材料把器物再一次产出；re- 标记第二次出现，而复制品本身就公开地处于次要地位。

senses.title: Rebuilding capital and labour
senses.titleCN: 再生产：经济体系把自身条件重新造出
senses.definition: the process by which an economy renews the capital, labour, and social relations it needs to continue
senses.definitionCN: 经济体系重新造出延续自身所需的资本、劳动力与社会关系的过程
senses.example: Marx argued that the wage relation secures the reproduction of labour power.
senses.exampleCN: 马克思主张，工资关系保证了劳动力的再生产。
senses.why: In economics the object reproduced is not a thing but the conditions of production; the system produces the means of producing again.
senses.whyCN: 在经济学中，被再生产的不是某件物品，而是生产条件本身；体系产出的是“再次生产的手段”。

senses.title: Bringing a scene back
senses.titleCN: 再现：把声音、画面或情境重放出来
senses.definition: the act of recreating a sound, image, or situation so that it can be experienced again
senses.definitionCN: 把声音、图像或情境重新造出，使人能再次体验
senses.example: The recording gives a faithful reproduction of the concert hall's acoustics.
senses.exampleCN: 这段录音忠实再现了音乐厅的声学效果。
senses.why: Here the thing reproduced is an experience rather than an object; fidelity is judged by how little the listener notices the medium.
senses.whyCN: 这里复制的是体验而不是物件；还原的忠実程度，取决于听众多不容易察觉媒介的存在。

senses.title: How well sound or colour comes back
senses.titleCN: 还原度：音响与色彩的再现质量
senses.definition: the quality with which a recording or display recreates sound or colour
senses.definitionCN: 录音或显示设备重现声音或色彩的质量
senses.example: Cheap speakers give poor reproduction of low notes.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价音箱对低音的还原很差。
senses.why: The word shifts from the act to the standard of the result: a system has good reproduction when little of the original is lost.
senses.whyCN: 词义从动作转到结果的标准：当原物损失很少时，系统就有良好的还原度。

senses.title: Breeding behaviour
senses.titleCN: 生殖活动：求偶、产卵与育幼
senses.definition: the behaviour and timing by which animals or plants breed
senses.definitionCN: 动物或植物繁殖的行为与时间安排
senses.example: Day length triggers reproduction in many temperate birds.
senses.exampleCN: 日照长度触发许多温带鸟类的生殖活动。
senses.why: Reproduction as a countable, seasonal event is the biological process seen from the calendar rather than from the cell.
senses.whyCN: 作为可按季节计数的事件，这一义项是从日历而不是从细胞层面看繁殖过程。

senses.title: Copying documents
senses.titleCN: 翻印：文件与图像的机械复制
senses.definition: the mechanical copying of documents, images, or recordings
senses.definitionCN: 对文件、图像或录音的机械复制
senses.example: The archive restricts reproduction of fragile manuscripts.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆限制对易损手稿的翻印。
senses.why: Printing and photography detached copying from the hand; reproduction then names an industrial service rather than a likeness made by an artist.
senses.whyCN: 印刷与摄影把手工复制与原件分离；reproduction 由此指一种工业服务，而不是艺术家的仿作。

senses.title: Passing inequality along
senses.titleCN: 社会再生产：把不平等传给下一代
senses.definition: in sociology, the way families and schools transmit advantage and disadvantage across generations
senses.definitionCN: 社会学中指家庭与学校把优势与劣势跨代传递的方式
senses.example: The study examines the reproduction of class differences through schooling.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究考察阶级差异如何通过学校教育被再生产。
senses.why: Society reproduces itself by reproducing its divisions; nothing is copied deliberately, yet the pattern returns.
senses.whyCN: 社会通过再生产自身的分层来延续自身；没有人刻意复制，格局却照样重现。

intro.en: Reproduction is re- plus production. Production goes back to Latin producere, to lead forth, from pro-, forward, and ducere, to lead.
intro.cn: reproduction 是 re- 加 production。production 可追溯到拉丁语 producere“引出、带出”，由 pro-“向前”与 ducere“引导”构成。

items.en: Ducere meant to lead or draw. Nearly every English word in this family carries the image of something being led out into view.
items.cn: ducere 意为“引导、牵引”。这一词族的英语词几乎都带着“把某物引出到眼前”的形象。

items.en: Producere joined pro-, forward, with ducere: to lead or bring forth, as a plant brings forth a shoot.
items.cn: producere 由 pro-“向前”与 ducere 组合：引出、带出，如同植物长出枝条。

items.en: Productio named a lengthening or a bringing forth; the noun kept the sense of extending something out from a source.
items.cn: productio 指拉长或引出；这个名词保留了“从源头把某物延伸出来”的意思。

items.en: English production first meant the act of bringing forth goods, plays, or arguments; the thing produced is secondary to the act.
items.cn: 英语 production 最初指产出货物、演出戏剧或提出论据的行为；被产出之物相对于动作是次要的。

items.en: The prefix re- means back or again. Added to production it marks a second bringing forth, whether of offspring or of copies.
items.cn: 前缀 re- 表示“回、再”。加在 production 上就标记第二次产出，无论产出的是后代还是复制品。

items.en: Reproduction is recorded in the 18th century for the generation of new organisms, and soon after for copies of artworks and printed matter.
items.cn: reproduction 的书面记录见于 18 世纪，指新个体的产生；不久后又指艺术品与印刷品的复制品。

note.en: The first group shares the produce root but differs in grammatical role; the second compares words for copies and for breeding.
note.cn: 第一组共享 produce 词根，但语法角色不同；第二组比较表示复制与繁殖的几个词。

entries.definition: to produce offspring or make a copy. It names the action.
entries.definitionCN: 繁殖或复制；命名的是动作。

entries.definition: relating to breeding or to copying. It describes what serves reproduction.
entries.definitionCN: 与繁殖或复制有关的；描述服务于繁殖或复制的事物。

entries.definition: able to be made again, especially of an experiment. It judges repeatability.
entries.definitionCN: 能够被再次做出的，尤指实验；评判的是可重复性。

entries.definition: an imitation of an original. It is the everyday word and carries no scientific sense.
entries.definitionCN: 对原件的仿制；是日常用词，不含科学含义。

entries.definition: an exact second version made for practical use, such as a spare key.
entries.definitionCN: 为实用目的做出的完全相同的第二份，如备用钥匙。

entries.definition: the controlled production of animals or plants by humans. It stresses human management.
entries.definitionCN: 人类对动植物繁殖的控制；强调人为管理。

entries.definition: the copying of a process or molecule, especially in science. It stresses exact repetition of a mechanism.
entries.definitionCN: 过程或分子的复制，尤用于科学；强调机制的精确重复。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: re-, production. Production comes from Latin producere, to lead forth, so reproduction is leading forth again.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：re- 与 production。production 出自拉丁语 producere“引出”，所以 reproduction 就是“再一次引出”。

normal.en: Re plus production: bring the same thing forth a second time.
normal.cn: re 加 production：把同样的东西第二次产出。

normal.en: A rabbit reproducing is a species bringing itself forth again.
normal.cn: 兔子繁殖，就是一个物种把自己再一次产出。

normal.en: A museum reproduction is an honest second body for an object that must stay safe.
normal.cn: 博物馆复制品是替必须妥善保存的原件做出的诚实的第二个身体。

normal.en: Good speakers have good reproduction: little of the original sound is lost.
normal.cn: 好音箱的还原度好：原声损失很少。

normal.en: Photocopying a manuscript is reproduction in the office, not in the greenhouse.
normal.cn: 复印手稿是办公室里的复制，不是温室里的繁殖。

abstract.en: Every copy is a claim about what mattered in the original.
abstract.cn: 每一件复制品都是关于“原件里什么才重要”的一次主张。

abstract.en: A society reproduces itself most quietly when nobody notices the pattern returning.
abstract.cn: 社会最安静地再生产自身的时刻，是没人注意到旧格局又回来的时候。

abstract.en: Reproduction without variation would end adaptation; copying always carries small errors.
abstract.cn: 没有变异的复制会终止适应；复制总带着微小的错误。

examples.en: Bacteria reproduce by splitting, so a single cell can found a colony in hours.
examples.cn: 细菌靠分裂繁殖，一个细胞数小时内就能建立菌落。

examples.en: The gallery sells reproductions of the frescoes to protect the originals from flash photography.
examples.cn: 美术馆出售壁画复制品，以保护原件不受闪光灯损害。

examples.en: The paper failed to report enough detail for reproduction of the experiment.
examples.cn: 这篇论文未报告足够细节，实验无法被重复。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（再）+ production（生产）——再生一次，既可指生后代，也可指复制品。

root: 由 re-（再、重新）加 production（产出，源自拉丁语 producere“引出”，由 pro-“向前”与 ducere“引导”构成）组合而成，本义为“把同一事物再一次产出”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of reproduction, all circling one idea: the same form comes back. What returns may be an organism, a copy, a set of economic conditions, a sound, colour fidelity, a seasonal brood, a printed page, or a social pattern.
sensesIntro.cn: reproduction 的八个义项都围绕一个观念：同一形制再次出现。回来的可以是生物个体、复制品、经济条件、声音、色彩还原、季节性繁殖、印刷页面，也可以是社会格局。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three identical seedlings beside the mother plant in a greenhouse, every leaf vein matching.
core.cn: 核心意象：温室里母株旁并排三株一模一样的小苗，叶脉纹路全都相同。

chain: ENGLISH PRODUCTION THE ACT OF MAKING

branches.en: LIVING REPRODUCTION: the making of new individuals and the seasonal behaviour that times it.
branches.cn: 生命繁衍：新个体的产生，以及为之定时序的生殖活动。

branches.en: COPIES OF THINGS: an art reproduction and a photocopied document, both openly second-hand.
branches.cn: 物品的复制：艺术复制品与复印文件，都公开地是二手之物。

branches.en: SYSTEMS REPRODUCING THEMSELVES: capital and labour renewed, and social divisions passed on.
branches.cn: 体系自我延续：资本与劳动力的更新，以及社会分层的传递。

branches.en: AN EXPERIENCE BROUGHT BACK: a recorded scene that a listener can enter again.
branches.cn: 体验的再现：被记录的场面，让听者得以再次进入。

branches.en: FIDELITY AS A STANDARD: the measured quality of sound or colour returned.
branches.cn: 作为标准的还原度：声音或色彩被送回时的可测质量。

intro.en: Reproduction is re- plus production. The family includes the verb reproduce and the adjectives reproductive and reproducible, with -tion, -ive, and -ible doing different work.
intro.cn: reproduction 是 re- 加 production。词族包括动词 reproduce 以及形容词 reproductive 与 reproducible，其中 -tion、-ive、-ible 各司其职。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is ducere, with producere and productio above it. The prefix re- is Latin and the -tion suffix reaches English through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 ducere，其上是 producere 与 productio。前缀 re- 来自拉丁语，后缀 -tion 经法语进入英语。

items.example: The same root appears in duct, reduce, and conduct.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根出现在 duct（管道）、reduce（减少）、conduct（引导）等词中。

items.example: The Latin verb could describe a tree putting out new growth.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词可以描述树木长出新枝。

items.structure: Latin producere through English verb formation
items.meaning: to make, grow, or bring into being
items.example: The region produces most of the country's rice.
items.exampleCN: 该国大部分稻米产自这个地区。

items.meaning: the act of making goods or works
items.example: Steel production fell for a second year.
items.exampleCN: 钢产量连续第二年下降。

items.meaning: to breed, or to make a copy
items.example: Some lizards reproduce without males.
items.exampleCN: 有些蜥蜴无需雄性即可繁殖。

items.meaning: the process or result of producing again
items.example: The archive keeps a reproduction of every fragile map.
items.exampleCN: 档案馆为每张易损地图保存一份复制品。

items.example: The frog's reproductive cycle depends on seasonal rain.
items.exampleCN: 这种蛙的生殖周期取决于季节性降雨。

items.meaning: able to be made again or copied
items.example: A reproducible result is the minimum standard in experimental science.
items.exampleCN: 可重现的结果是实验科学的最低标准。

items.example: The journal now asks authors for a reproducibility statement.
items.exampleCN: 该期刊现在要求作者提交可复现性声明。

definition_zh: n. 谴责，责难；v. 正式谴责
definition_en: strong official or public disapproval; to express strong disapproval of someone
core_image: 议会席间一片低声的斥责
scene: 议员们以投票正式谴责了这位部长的行为。 The members voted to censure the minister for his conduct.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：censure 指谴责；句意是议员投票正式谴责部长的行为。

senses.title: Formal disapproval
senses.definition: strong official disapproval expressed in public
senses.definitionCN: 公开表达的强烈官方不满
senses.example: The committee issued a censure.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会发出正式谴责。
senses.why: The word comes from Latin censura, the office of a censor.
senses.whyCN: 该词来自拉丁语 censura（监察官之职）。

senses.title: To condemn formally
senses.definition: to express formal disapproval of a person or act
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某行为表达正式不满
senses.example: The senate censured him by a clear majority.
senses.exampleCN: 参议院以明显多数谴责了他。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb without change.
senses.whyCN: 名词原样转为动词。

intro.en: Censure comes from Latin censura, the office and judgment of a censor.
intro.cn: censure 来自拉丁语 censura，指监察官的职位与评判。

items.en: Censura names a censors office.
items.cn: censura 指监察官的职位。

items.en: English censure means judgment.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语指评判。

items.en: Parliament uses censure for formal blame.
items.cn: 十七世纪议会用 censure 指正式责备。

items.en: Church courts issue censures.
items.cn: 十八世纪教会法庭发出谴责。

items.en: Censure means official public blame.
items.cn: 现代指官方公开谴责。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cens- opening; the near-meaning group ranks blame from plain to formal.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cens- 开头；近义组把责备从平常排到正式。

entries.definition: An official who removes material.
entries.definitionCN: 审查员。

entries.definition: An official count of people.
entries.definitionCN: 人口普查。

entries.definition: To make certain.
entries.definitionCN: 确保。

entries.definition: Responsibility for a fault.
entries.definitionCN: 责备。

entries.definition: A sharp expression of disapproval.
entries.definitionCN: 斥责。

entries.definition: To say strongly that something is wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 谴责。

normalIntro.en: A censure is blame that has been written into the minutes.
normalIntro.cn: censure 是被写进会议记录的责备。

normal.en: Censura was a censors judgment.
normal.cn: censura 是监察官的评判。

normal.en: A censure is formal public blame.
normal.cn: censure 是正式的公开责备。

normal.en: Parliaments pass motions of censure.
normal.cn: 议会通过谴责动议。

normal.en: The verb means to condemn officially.
normal.cn: 动词义为正式谴责。

normal.en: The tone is always serious.
normal.cn: 语气总是严肃的。

abstract.en: A raised hand that says no.
abstract.cn: 一只表示否定的举手。

abstract.en: Disapproval entered in a ledger.
abstract.cn: 记进账簿的不满。

abstract.en: A cold word in a warm room.
abstract.cn: 暖房里的一句冷话。

examples.en: The council passed a vote of censure.
examples.cn: 委员会通过了谴责表决。

examples.en: She was censured for the leak.
examples.cn: 她因泄密受到谴责。

examples.en: Censures of this kind rarely change policy.
examples.cn: 这类谴责很少改变政策。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「森舍」——森林般密集的斥责，把人舍在中间。

root: 拉丁语 censura（监察官之职）→ 英语 censure

sensesIntro.en: The judgment of an office became the public blame of a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 官职的评判变成了对人的公开责备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a formal rebuke read into the record
core.cn: 核心意象：被宣读进记录的正式斥责

branches.en: A motion read aloud in a chamber.
branches.cn: 在议事厅宣读的动议。

branches.en: A headline that names the fault.
branches.cn: 点明过失的标题。

branches.en: A majority raising its hands.
branches.cn: 举起手的多数人。

branches.en: A minister answering in silence.
branches.cn: 沉默作答的部长。

branches.en: Blame given an official voice.
branches.cn: 获得官方声音的责备。

intro.en: Censure has a Latin root; the list below adds words for judgment, blame and formal speech.
intro.cn: censure 有拉丁词根；下面列出评判、责备、正式言词词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin censura is judgment, and iudicium is a verdict.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 censura 意为评判，iudicium 意为裁决。

definition_zh: 地峡；峡部；狭窄的连接通道
definition_en: a narrow strip of land joining two larger areas of land, with water on both sides
core_image: 两块大陆之间一条窄窄的陆桥，两侧都是海
scene: 一条运河横穿地峡。 A canal cuts across the isthmus.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「连接两块陆地的狭长地带」（第 1 个义项：两侧临水的陆桥）；句意为一条运河横穿地峡。

senses.title: A narrow neck of land
senses.titleCN: 地峡：连接两块陆地的狭长地带
senses.definition: a narrow strip of land with water on both sides that joins two larger land areas
senses.definitionCN: 两侧临水、连接两块较大陆地的狭长地带
senses.example: A canal cuts across the isthmus.
senses.exampleCN: 一条运河横穿地峡。
senses.why: Greek isthmos named a narrow passage, first the neck at Corinth, where land is the passage between two seas.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语原指狭窄通道，最初是科林斯的地颈，那里陆地成了两海之间的通道。

senses.title: The isthmus zone
senses.definition: the whole strip of land and its immediate surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 整条陆地狭带及其周边
senses.example: Roads and railways crowd the isthmus zone.
senses.exampleCN: 公路与铁路挤满了地峡地带。
senses.why: Planners treat more than the neck itself as a zone because traffic concentrates there.
senses.whyCN: 规划者把地颈以外的一带也算作区域，因为交通在此集中。

senses.title: A narrow part in anatomy
senses.definition: a narrow passage joining two larger parts of an organ
senses.definitionCN: 连接器官两个较大部分之间的狭窄通道
senses.example: The auditory isthmus links the middle ear to the throat.
senses.exampleCN: 耳峡把中耳与咽部连接起来。
senses.why: Anatomy borrowed the land image for any narrow joining passage in the body.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学借用了陆地意象，指身体内任何狭窄的连接通道。

senses.title: A narrow link between fields
senses.titleCN: 比喻：两个领域之间的窄连接
senses.definition: a narrow connection between two otherwise separate fields or systems
senses.definitionCN: 两个原本分离的领域或系统之间的狭窄连接
senses.example: A single road is the isthmus between the two towns.
senses.exampleCN: 一条路就是两镇之间的地峡。
senses.why: Any narrow link carrying traffic between two bodies can be pictured as an isthmus.
senses.whyCN: 任何在两个主体之间输送往来的狭窄连接，都能被想象成地峡。

senses.title: A canal across an isthmus
senses.definition: a waterway cut through an isthmus to join the seas on either side
senses.definitionCN: 穿过地峡、连接两侧海域的水道
senses.example: The isthmus canal shortened the voyage by weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 这条地峡运河把航程缩短了几周。
senses.why: An isthmus blocks ships, so cutting it turns land passage into water passage.
senses.whyCN: 地峡阻挡船只，切开它就把它从陆上通道变成水上通道。

senses.title: A strategic choke point
senses.definition: a narrow land passage of military or commercial importance
senses.definitionCN: 具有军事或商业重要性的狭窄陆上通道
senses.example: Armies fought for control of the isthmus.
senses.exampleCN: 军队争夺这条地峡的控制权。
senses.why: Because everything must pass through the neck, control of it controls movement.
senses.whyCN: 因为一切都要经过这条地颈，控制它就控制了往来。

senses.title: A land bridge in geography
senses.definition: a broad land connection between continents, especially in the geological past
senses.definitionCN: 大陆之间宽阔的陆地连接，尤指地质历史上的
senses.example: The isthmus once let animals cross between the continents.
senses.exampleCN: 这条地峡曾让动物在两块大陆之间通行。
senses.why: A land bridge is the larger, historical version of an isthmus; scale and time separate the terms.
senses.whyCN: 陆桥是地峡更大、更具历史尺度的版本；规模与时间区分二者。

senses.title: How an isthmus forms
senses.definition: a land connection built by sediment or by the meeting of two shores
senses.definitionCN: 由沉积物堆积或两岸相接而形成的陆地连接
senses.example: Sand built the isthmus that now joins the island.
senses.exampleCN: 沙子堆积成地峡，如今把岛与大陆连在一起。
senses.why: Currents and sediment can close a gap, which is one physical way an isthmus appears.
senses.whyCN: 水流与沉积物能填满缺口，这是地峡出现的物理方式之一。

intro.en: Isthmus comes from Greek isthmos, a narrow passage, first used of the neck at Corinth. Its deeper origin is uncertain. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 该词来自希腊语，意为狭窄通道，最初用于科林斯地颈。其更深来源并不确定。年代均为约数。

items.en: isthmos meant 'narrow passage, neck of land', and it first named the Corinthian isthmus.
items.cn: 希腊语词意为「狭窄通道、地颈」，最初指科林斯地峡。

items.en: Its deeper origin is uncertain: one suggestion links it to a verb 'to go', another to 'to stand', and neither is proved.
items.cn: 其更深来源不确定：有人把它与表示「走」的动词联系，也有人与表示「站立」的词联系，两种说法都未获证明。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word as isthmus without changing its meaning, so the Latin form is a loan, not a native root.
items.cn: 拉丁语原样借入这个希腊词，意义未变，因此拉丁形式是借词，不是本族词根。

items.en: English took the Latin form in the sixteenth century and applied it to narrow land bridges elsewhere.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入拉丁形式，并把它用于其他地方的狭窄陆桥。

items.en: The same narrow-passage image was applied to organs, giving the anatomical sense of a narrow joining part.
items.cn: 同一「狭窄通道」意象被用于器官，产生解剖学中狭窄连接部分的义项。

items.en: Source uncertain (origin): several hypotheses exist and no single root is agreed; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根）：存在多种假说，学界未就单一词根达成一致；英语首见年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike forms of the same Greek word; group two holds the geographic terms most often confused with an isthmus.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个希腊词的形近形式；第二组是最容易与地峡混淆的地理术语。

entries.definition: Relating to an isthmus, especially the Corinthian one; it is the adjective while the noun names the land.
entries.definitionCN: 指与地峡有关的，尤指科林斯地峡；它是形容词，而名词指陆地。

entries.definition: Relating to a narrow joining part, especially in anatomy; it is the technical adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指与狭窄连接部分有关的，尤用于解剖；它是技术形容词。

entries.definition: A condition of difficult breathing; it shares some letters and sounds but has a different Greek origin.
entries.definitionCN: 指呼吸困难的疾病；部分字母与读音相同，但希腊来源不同。

entries.definition: A wide land connection between continents, often of the geological past; an isthmus is narrower and present-day.
entries.definitionCN: 指大陆之间宽阔的陆地连接，常属地质历史；地峡更窄且多为现今存在。

entries.definition: The narrow part joining a head to a body, or any narrow joining part; it is the plain everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 指连接头与身体的狭窄部分，或任何狭窄连接处；它是平实的日常词。

entries.definition: A narrow passage of water between two lands; it is the water counterpart of an isthmus.
entries.definitionCN: 指两片陆地之间的狭窄水道；它是地峡的水上对应物。

entries.definition: Land almost surrounded by water; it projects rather than joins two masses.
entries.definitionCN: 指几乎被水包围的陆地；它是向外突出，而非连接两块陆地。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The original sense is 'narrow passage', and land is the passage between two seas.
normal.cn: 原义是「狭窄通道」，而陆地就是两海之间的通道。

normal.en: The family runs isthmus, isthmian, isthmic, isthmus canal and isthmus neck.
normal.cn: 同族词包括本词、地峡形容词、峡部形容词、地峡运河与地峡颈部。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: the Isthmus of Panama, a narrow isthmus, an isthmus canal.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：巴拿马地峡、狭窄地峡、地峡运河。

normal.en: The contrast to remember is simple: an isthmus is land between waters, a strait is water between lands.
normal.cn: 要记住的对比很简单：地峡是水之间的陆地，海峡是陆地之间的水。

normal.en: Anatomy uses the same image for any narrow joining part of an organ.
normal.cn: 解剖学用同一意象指器官内任何狭窄的连接部分。

abstract.en: Picture a thin bridge of stone joining two wide rooms.
abstract.cn: 想象一条窄窄的石桥连着两个宽房间。

abstract.en: Picture a short corridor that is the only way between two halls.
abstract.cn: 想象一条短走廊，是两座大厅之间唯一的通道。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow waist joining two larger parts of a body.
abstract.cn: 想象一条窄腰连接身体两个较宽的部分。

examples.en: The isthmus is only a few kilometres wide at its narrowest point.
examples.cn: 这条地峡最窄处只有几公里宽。

examples.en: Traffic between the two seas must cross the isthmus by rail.
examples.cn: 两海之间的往来必须靠铁路穿过地峡。

examples.en: The isthmus of the thyroid joins its two lobes.
examples.cn: 甲状腺峡部连接它的两个叶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一死没死」：地峡窄得只剩一条路，人挤着也要过去。

root: 希腊语 isthmos「狭窄通道、地颈」，最初指科林斯地峡；更深词根存疑，主要有「走」与「站立」两种未证实假说。拉丁语只是借入，英语 isthmus。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one narrow link: land joining two larger masses across water. The link is then widened into a zone, narrowed to an organ, used as a metaphor, cut by a canal, fought over, compared with a land bridge and explained as a formation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条狭窄连接展开：陆地跨水连接两块较大陆地。这条连接随后被扩成地带、收窄到器官、用作比喻、被运河切开、成为争夺对象、与陆桥比较，并被解释为一种形成过程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow land bridge with sea on both sides, the only dry route between two masses.
core.cn: 核心意象：两侧是海的狭长陆桥，是两块陆地之间唯一的旱路。

branches.en: THE LINK: a present-day neck and a prehistoric land bridge are the same idea at different scales.
branches.cn: 连接：现今地颈与史前陆桥是同一观念的不同尺度。

branches.en: THE ZONE: traffic and sediment both gather around the narrow strip.
branches.cn: 地带：交通与沉积物都聚集在这条狭带上。

branches.en: THE BODY: anatomy borrows the image for any narrow joining part.
branches.cn: 身体：解剖学借这个意象指任何狭窄连接部分。

branches.en: CONTROL: a narrow link funnels movement, which makes it strategic.
branches.cn: 控制：狭窄连接把往来集中起来，因此具有战略意义。

branches.en: THE CUT: a canal turns the land link into a water route.
branches.cn: 切开：运河把陆地连接变成水上通道。

intro.en: Isthmus is a Greek loan with almost no productive English morphology; its family is small and technical.
intro.cn: 该词是希腊语借词，在英语中几乎不产生新词，词族小而偏技术。

latinIntro.en: Latin only borrowed the Greek word, so there is no Latin root family and the Latin entry list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语只是借入这个希腊词，没有拉丁词根词族，因此拉丁词条列表留空。

items.exampleCN: 巴拿马地峡连接两块大陆。

definition_zh: 解密；把密文还原为可读内容的过程
definition_en: the process of turning coded information back into readable form
core_image: 一只带锁的圆筒被打开，卷在里面的信纸展开，原本的字迹一行行重新出现
scene: 档案馆里，管理员转动钥匙，屏幕上那团乱码渐渐还原成一封完整的旧信。 With the right key, decryption restored the letter to plain words in a few seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 decryption 指把密文还原成可读内容的过程（第 1 个义项：还原这一动作）；句意：用对了钥匙，解密在几秒内就把那封信恢复成明白的话。

pos.zh: 解密；密文还原；解密过程

senses.title: The act of restoring plain text
senses.titleCN: 把密文还原成明文的动作
senses.definition: the act of applying the reversing procedure that turns code back into readable text
senses.definitionCN: 执行逆向程序、把代码变回可读文本的动作
senses.example: Decryption happens inside the phone, not on the server.
senses.exampleCN: 解密发生在手机内部，而不是服务器上。
senses.why: the noun names the action first, the way construction names both the act and the thing built.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词首先指动作，正如 construction 同时指建造与建筑。

senses.title: The recovered message
senses.definition: the readable text produced once the code is undone
senses.definitionCN: 代码被解除后得到的可读文本
senses.example: The decryption was a single line of ordinary invoice text.
senses.exampleCN: 解密出来的内容只有一行普通的发票文字。
senses.why: the same action noun stands for its product, so one can hold the decryption in one's hand.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动作名词也指其产物，所以可以说「拿到解密出来的内容」。

senses.title: The technical discipline
senses.definition: the part of cryptography concerned with reversing transformations and proving they work
senses.definitionCN: 密码学中负责逆转变换并验证其有效性的部分
senses.example: Their paper compares decryption costs across three schemes.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的论文比较了三种方案下的解密开销。
senses.why: a repeated technical operation is studied as a subject, and the process noun becomes its name.
senses.whyCN: 反复进行的技术操作会被当作学科研究，过程名词就成了它的名称。

senses.title: Authorised access to stored data
senses.titleCN: 对存档数据的授权读取
senses.definition: the routine unfolding of protected files for a user who holds the key
senses.definitionCN: 持钥匙的用户把受保护文件照常展开
senses.example: Decryption of the archive is logged every time an archivist opens it.
senses.exampleCN: 档案员每次打开档案，解密操作都会被记录。
senses.why: protection at rest would be useless without a legal path back, and that path is named by this word.
senses.whyCN: 静态保护若没有合法的回路就毫无意义，这个词就是那条回路的名称。

senses.title: Reading intercepted traffic
senses.definition: the successful restoration of a message that was captured in transit
senses.definitionCN: 把传输中被截获的消息成功还原
senses.example: Their decryption of the signal exposed a planned shipment.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对信号的解密暴露了一批计划中的货运。
senses.why: the word is neutral about who holds the key, so it also names the eavesdropper's success.
senses.whyCN: 这个词对持钥匙者是谁保持中立，因此也指窃听者的成功。

senses.title: Historical reading of old ciphers
senses.definition: the scholarly recovery of hand-written cipher text from the past
senses.definitionCN: 学界对古代手写密文的还原
senses.example: The decryption of the royal letters took two scholars a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 两位学者花了十年才解开那批王室信件。
senses.why: old documents still wait for keys, and historians use the modern noun for that labour.
senses.whyCN: 旧文献仍在等钥匙，历史学者便用这个现代名词来称这项工作。

senses.title: The key mechanism in reverse
senses.definition: the paired rule and secret value that allow the transformation to be undone
senses.definitionCN: 使变换得以撤销的成对规则与秘密数值
senses.example: Symmetric decryption uses the same key that sealed the file.
senses.exampleCN: 对称解密使用封存文件时的同一把钥匙。
senses.why: people name the machinery by its effect, so the reverse effect names the reverse machinery.
senses.whyCN: 人们按效果命名机器，反向的效果就命名了反向的机器。

senses.title: Figurative clarification
senses.definition: the figurative act of making an obscure statement plain again
senses.definitionCN: 把晦涩的说法重新讲明白的比喻用法
senses.example: Her footnote was a quiet decryption of the chairman's speech.
senses.exampleCN: 她的脚注是对主席讲话的一次悄然解读。
senses.why: once code is undone, obscurity becomes sense, and any puzzling statement can borrow the image.
senses.whyCN: 代码一旦解掉，晦涩就变回意义，任何难解的说法都能借用这个意象。

intro.en: Decryption is the mirror of encryption: the Latin prefix de-, meaning reversal, placed before the Greek hidden root and closed with the Latin action ending.
intro.cn: decryption 是 encryption 的镜像：拉丁前缀 de- 表示反向，放在希腊「隐藏」词根之前，再以拉丁动作词尾收束。

items.en: Greek kryptos, hidden, and kryptein, to hide, supplied the root that all these words share.
items.cn: 希腊语 kryptos「隐藏的」与 kryptein「隐藏」提供了这一族词共享的词根。

items.en: Latin crypta named a covered vault, and its English descendant crypt still means an underground room.
items.cn: 拉丁语 crypta 指有顶的拱室，其英语后裔 crypt 至今仍指地下空间。

items.en: Latin de- meant down from or away, and in verbs it came to mark undoing, so it is the natural prefix for opening what was closed.
items.cn: 拉丁语 de- 表示「向下、离开」，在动词中逐渐表示「撤销」，因此天然适合表示「把封上的东西打开」。

items.en: English built encrypt and then decrypt on the same root, so the two verbs stand as a matched pair of opposite actions.
items.cn: 英语在同一词根上先后造出 encrypt 与 decrypt，两个动词构成一对相反动作。

items.en: Twentieth-century signalling and computing fixed the noun decryption for the reverse operation, parallel to encryption.
items.cn: 二十世纪的通信与计算把名词 decryption 固定指反向操作，与 encryption 平行。

items.en: Source uncertain: the earliest history of the Greek root is unsettled, and the forms sometimes compared with it are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个希腊词根最早的历史没有定论，常被比较的形式属于重构形式。

note.en: The first group is the same root in its other shapes; the second group is the neighbouring ways of making something readable.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词根的其他形式；第二组是使内容变得可读的相邻说法。

entries.definition: To carry out the reversal; the noun names the process or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 指执行还原动作；名词指过程或其结果。

entries.definition: The outward journey into code; decryption is the homeward journey.
entries.definitionCN: 指进入代码的去程；decryption 是回程。

entries.definition: Having been converted back to a readable form, used of messages and signals.
entries.definitionCN: 指已被还原成可读形式，多用于消息与信号。

entries.definition: Deliberately obscure in meaning, with no key involved.
entries.definitionCN: 指故意晦涩难解，不涉及密钥。

entries.definition: Turning a representation back into ordinary form by a public rule; no secret key is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 按公开规则把某种表示换回普通形式，不需要秘密密钥。

entries.definition: Working out a cipher without being told the rule; decryption usually assumes the key is known.
entries.definitionCN: 在不知规则的情况下破译密码；decryption 通常假定钥匙已知。

entries.definition: Opening a lock; the everyday image behind the technical operation.
entries.definitionCN: 打开锁；是这一技术操作背后的日常意象。

entries.definition: Explaining what a statement means; it works on ambiguity rather than on symbols.
entries.definitionCN: 解释某句话的意思；处理的是歧义，而不是符号。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations from the real prefix, the real pair and the real phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：来自真实前缀、真实对立词与真实搭配。

normal.en: de- marks reversal, so decryption is encryption run backwards.
normal.cn: de- 表示反向，因此 decryption 就是倒着跑的 encryption。

normal.en: The pair is fixed: encryption key to lock, decryption key to open.
normal.cn: 这一对固定成套：加密密钥上锁，解密密钥开锁。

normal.en: The verb is regular: decrypts, decrypted, decrypted, decrypting.
normal.cn: 动词变化规则：decrypts、decrypted、decrypted、decrypting。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: decryption key, decryption process, decryption algorithm.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：解密密钥、解密过程、解密算法。

normal.en: If the key is lost, decryption is impossible even with the file in hand.
normal.cn: 钥匙一旦丢失，即使文件在手也无法解密。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed cylinder opening and the page inside remembering how to be a page.
abstract.cn: 想象封住的圆筒打开，里面的纸想起自己该怎么当一张纸。

abstract.en: Picture gravel slowly reassembling into handwriting on a table.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上的碎石慢慢重组成手写的字迹。

abstract.en: Picture a door that only opens for the person who remembers the word it was built with.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，只为记得它被造出时那句话的人打开。

examples.en: Decryption of the backup took less than a minute.
examples.cn: 备份的解密用了不到一分钟。

examples.en: The service performs decryption on the user's own device.
examples.cn: 这项服务在用户自己的设备上完成解密。

examples.en: Without the second key, decryption of the archive remains out of reach.
examples.cn: 没有第二把钥匙，档案的解密始终遥不可及。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「敌（de）刻入扑（cryption）」——把敌人刻进去的乱码扑开，就是解密

root: 希腊 kryptos「隐藏的」→ 拉丁 crypta「拱室」→ 英语 crypt；加拉丁前缀 de-「反向」与 -tion 构成 decryption，与 encryption 构成一对相反过程。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the plain reversal to its product, its discipline, its lawful use, its unlawful use, the historical craft, the key mechanism and the figurative reading.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从单纯的还原动作出发，走向产物、学科、合法用途、非授权用途、历史技艺、密钥机制与比喻性解读。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a locked cylinder opened, the page inside unfolding as its letters return.
core.cn: 核心意象：带锁的圆筒被打开，里面的纸展开，字迹重新回来。

branches.en: ACT AND PRODUCT: the reversal performed, and the readable text it yields.
branches.cn: 动作与产物：执行的还原动作，以及它产出的可读文本。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE AND MECHANISM: the studied branch of cryptography, and the key rule that permits reversal.
branches.cn: 学科与机制：被研究的密码学分支，以及允许逆转的密钥规则。

branches.en: LAWFUL USE: daily opening of protected archives by the person who holds the key.
branches.cn: 合法用途：持钥匙者日常打开受保护的档案。

branches.en: OTHER HANDS: intercepted traffic read by an outsider, and old ciphers read by scholars.
branches.cn: 他人之手：外人解读截获的通信，学者解读古代密码。

branches.en: FIGURATIVE CLARITY: an obscure public statement made plain again.
branches.cn: 比喻性的澄清：把晦涩的公开说法重新讲明白。

intro.en: Decryption combines a Latin reversing prefix, a Greek hidden root and a Latin action ending, with English participles attached to the verb.
intro.cn: decryption 由拉丁反向前缀、希腊「隐藏」词根与拉丁动作词尾组合而成，动词另带英语分词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Two Latin pieces are at work: de-, marking reversal, and -tion, marking an action noun; the root crypt- itself came to Latin from Greek.
latinIntro.cn: 这里有两个拉丁成分：de- 表示反向，-tion 表示动作名词；而 crypt- 词根本身是从希腊语进入拉丁语的。

items.example: The prefix turns the outward action into its reverse.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把向外的动作变成反向动作。

items.example: The adjective is the shared core of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是整个词族共享的核心。

items.example: The verb names the covering act that the code performs.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指代码所执行的遮盖动作。

items.example: Latin passed the hidden-place image to English.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把「隐蔽之处」的意象传给英语。

items.example: The ending names the reversal as a process.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把还原动作命名为过程。

items.example: The verb carries the action that the noun names.
items.exampleCN: 动词承载名词所指的动作。

items.example: A decrypted file has already been opened.
items.exampleCN: 已解密的文件已经被打开了。

items.example: Decrypting is the work in progress.
items.exampleCN: decrypting 指正在进行的工作。

items.meaning: one who or that which does
items.example: The ending marks a person or a device that performs it.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记执行该动作的人或装置。

definition_zh: 友好相待；与……交朋友；扶助
definition_en: to become a friend to someone, especially someone in need of help
core_image: 新来转学生的第一张课桌上，有人主动坐下陪她
scene: 转学生独自吃饭时，一个女孩端着托盘在她对面坐下。 The older students befriended the new girl at once.
sceneCN: 这里 befriended 是「友好相待、与之交朋友」（第 1 个义项：主动成为某人的朋友）；句意是高年级学生立刻与新来的女孩交上朋友。

derivatives.zh: 由 friend 加 -ship 构成，义为「友谊」
由 friend 加 -ly 构成，义为「友好的」
由 befriend 加 -er 构成，义为「陪伴帮扶者」

senses.title: To become a friend to someone
senses.definition: to act as a friend to someone, especially one who is new or alone
senses.definitionCN: 以朋友之道待人，尤指对待新来或孤独者
senses.example: The older students befriended the new girl at once.
senses.exampleCN: 高年级学生立刻与新来的女孩交上朋友。
senses.why: The be- prefix turns the noun friend into an action done towards a person.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 be- 把名词 friend 变为朝向他人的动作。

senses.title: To help or support charitably
senses.definition: to give practical help or comfort to someone in need
senses.definitionCN: 给困顿者以实际帮助或安慰
senses.example: A charity befriended hundreds of families after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后，一家慈善机构扶助了数以百计的家庭。
senses.why: Acting as a friend grew to include the duties of friendship, help and comfort.
senses.whyCN: 「以友相待」扩展到朋友之责，即帮助与安慰。

intro.en: Befriend puts the Old English prefix be- before friend.
intro.cn: befriend 在 friend 前加古英语前缀 be-。

items.en: freond meant friend, from freon, to love.
items.cn: 古英语 freond 意为「朋友」，源自 freon「爱」。

items.en: be- worked as a verb-making prefix.
items.cn: be- 是构成动词的前缀。

items.en: befrienden meant to act as a friend.
items.cn: 中古英语 befrienden 意为「以友相待」。

items.en: befriend was common in moral and religious writing.
items.cn: 十六世纪 befriend 常见于道德与宗教文字。

items.en: befriending services keep the charitable sense alive today.
items.cn: 如今的陪伴帮扶服务延续了其慈善义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the be- prefix or the friend root; the near-meaning group gathers words for aiding and welcoming.
note.cn: 形近组共享 be- 前缀或 friend 词根；近义组汇集帮助与接纳类词。

entries.definition: to cover with fog or confusion
entries.definitionCN: 使被雾笼罩；使困惑——同用 be- 前缀

entries.definition: to make a fool of
entries.definitionCN: 愚弄；同用 be- 前缀而意义相反

entries.definition: acting like a friend
entries.definitionCN: 友好的——同根形容词

entries.definition: to receive kindly
entries.definitionCN: 欢迎；强调接纳

entries.definition: to hold up or assist
entries.definitionCN: 支持；强调扶助

entries.definition: to accept readily and gladly
entries.definitionCN: 欣然接纳；强调情感接受

normalIntro.en: Befriend is be- plus friend: make a friend of someone.
normalIntro.cn: befriend 是 be- 加 friend：使某人成为朋友。

normal.en: The be- prefix makes nouns into verbs.
normal.cn: be- 前缀把名词变为动词。

normal.en: Befriended the lonely is a common use.
normal.cn: befriended the lonely 是常见用法。

normal.en: A befriending service offers companionship.
normal.cn: befriending service 提供陪伴服务。

normal.en: The root freond meant one who loves.
normal.cn: 词根 freond 意为「所爱之人」。

normal.en: Befool uses the same pattern, badly.
normal.cn: befool 用同样构词，却是贬义。

abstract.en: See a tray set down across an empty table.
abstract.cn: 想象一只托盘放到空桌对面。

abstract.en: Feel the first hour of a new school soften.
abstract.cn: 感受新学校第一个小时的紧张软化。

abstract.en: Picture a hand offered on a cold street.
abstract.cn: 想象寒街上伸出的一只手。
