definition_zh: 共价的；由原子共享电子对而形成的
definition_en: describing a bond in which two atoms share one or more pairs of electrons
core_image: 两只手各伸出一半，握住同一根绳，绳由两边共同持有
scene: 两个人各用一只手握住同一根绳的中段，绳身由两边共同持有。 Two atoms share a pair of electrons in a covalent bond.
sceneCN: 这里 covalent 指原子共享电子对而形成键的（第 1 个义项：以共享电子对为特征的键合）；句意：在共价键中两个原子共享一对电子。图中可辨识物件：一根绳、两只手、共同握住的绳段、绷紧的绳尾。

senses.title: Sharing electrons in a bond
senses.definition: describing a bond formed by two atoms sharing one or more pairs of electrons
senses.definitionCN: 指两个原子共享一对或多对电子而形成的键
senses.example: Two atoms share a pair of electrons in a covalent bond.
senses.exampleCN: 在共价键中两个原子共享一对电子。
senses.why: co- means together and the stem means strength or worth, so the word says that the two atoms hold the link jointly.
senses.whyCN: 前缀表示「共同」，词干表示「力量、价值」，因此这个词说的是两个原子共同持有这条连接。

senses.title: Of a covalently bonded compound
senses.titleCN: 由共价键构成的化合物
senses.definition: describing a compound whose atoms are joined mainly by shared-electron bonds
senses.definitionCN: 指原子主要由共享电子键连接的化合物
senses.example: Carbon dioxide is a covalent compound with no ions in it.
senses.exampleCN: 二氧化碳是一种共价化合物，其中没有离子。
senses.why: the adjective transferred from the bond to the whole substance that such bonds build.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从键转移到由这类键构成的整个物质。

senses.title: Covalent radius
senses.definition: describing the share of a bond length assigned to one atom when two atoms are joined covalently
senses.definitionCN: 指共价相连时分配给单个原子的那部分键长
senses.example: The covalent radius of chlorine is smaller than that of bromine.
senses.exampleCN: 氯的共价半径小于溴的共价半径。
senses.why: once bond lengths were measured, a half-length could be assigned to each atom, and the adjective marked that convention.
senses.whyCN: 键长可测之后，便可把一半长度分配给每个原子，这个形容词标记的正是这一约定。

senses.title: Covalent crystal
senses.definition: describing a solid held together in three dimensions by a continuous network of shared-electron bonds
senses.definitionCN: 指由共享电子键的连续网络在三维上维系的固体
senses.example: Diamond is a covalent crystal, which is why it scratches almost anything.
senses.exampleCN: 金刚石是共价晶体，所以它几乎能划伤任何东西。
senses.why: when the same bond repeats through a whole solid, the adjective moves from one link to the entire lattice.
senses.whyCN: 当同一种键贯穿整块固体重复出现，这个形容词便从一条连接转到整个晶格。

senses.title: Covalent modification in biochemistry
senses.titleCN: 生物化学中的共价修饰
senses.definition: describing a permanent chemical attachment of a group to a molecule, as in enzyme regulation
senses.definitionCN: 指某基团被化学性地永久接到分子上，如酶活性调节
senses.example: Phosphorylation is a covalent modification that switches the enzyme on.
senses.exampleCN: 磷酸化是一种共价修饰，能开启这种酶。
senses.why: biology borrowed the adjective for changes made by forming a real bond rather than by weak association.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借这个形容词指通过形成真实键、而非弱结合所造成的改变。

senses.title: Covalent catalysis
senses.definition: describing an enzyme mechanism in which a temporary covalent bond forms between enzyme and substrate
senses.definitionCN: 指酶与底物暂时形成共价键的催化机制
senses.example: The protease uses covalent catalysis to cut the peptide chain.
senses.exampleCN: 这种蛋白酶通过共价催化切断肽链。
senses.why: the mechanism is named by the kind of bond it uses, an ordinary extension of the adjective into a technique.
senses.whyCN: 这种机制以它所用的键型命名，是形容词向技术名称的普通延伸。

senses.title: Covalent cross-linking
senses.definition: describing permanent links formed between polymer chains to fix a network in place
senses.definitionCN: 指聚合物链之间形成的永久连接，使网络固定
senses.example: Covalent cross-linking makes the hydrogel keep its shape in water.
senses.exampleCN: 共价交联使水凝胶在水中保持形状。
senses.why: materials science describes a network by the kind of links that hold it, so the adjective precedes the joining.
senses.whyCN: 材料科学以维系网络的连接种类来描述网络，因此这个形容词放在「连接」之前。

senses.title: Covalent character in a bond
senses.definition: describing the degree to which a bond that is formally ionic still shares electrons
senses.definitionCN: 指形式上是离子键、实际仍共享电子的程度
senses.example: The bond in hydrogen chloride has substantial covalent character.
senses.exampleCN: 氯化氢中的键有相当大的共价成分。
senses.why: since real bonds fall between two extremes, the adjective became a measure of how far a bond leans toward sharing.
senses.whyCN: 由于真实的键处在两个极端之间，这个形容词便成为衡量键偏向共享程度的量。

intro.en: Covalent is a modern compound of co-, from Latin com-, together, and valent, from Latin valens, being strong or being worth. It was coined in English in the early twentieth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: covalent 是现代复合词，由 co-（出自拉丁 com-「共同」）与 valent（出自拉丁 valens「有力量、有价值」）构成。它在 20 世纪初由英语造出。年代均为约数。

items.en: Valere meant to be strong, to be well, to be worth; it also supplied value and valid. Its Indo-European connections are reconstructions.
items.cn: valere 意为「有力量、健康、有价值」，还给出 value 与 valid。它的印欧语联系属于重构。

items.en: The present participle valens, strong or worth, produced English words in -valent and the noun valentia, strength or capacity.
items.cn: 现在分词 valens「有力量的、有价值的」产生了英语中以 -valent 结尾的词，以及名词 valentia「力量、容量」。

items.en: Com-, together, assimilates to co- before vowels and to col-, cor- and con- before certain consonants, a pattern visible across the family.
items.cn: com-「共同」在元音前同化为 co-，在某些辅音前同化为 col-、cor-、con-，这一模式在整个词族中可见。

items.en: Nineteenth-century chemistry took valence from Latin valentia for the combining capacity of an atom, the quantity that covalent later qualified.
items.cn: 19 世纪的化学从拉丁 valentia 取来 valence，指原子的化合能力，也就是 covalent 后来所限定的那个量。

items.en: Covalent and covalence were coined in the early twentieth century, when chemists needed a word for bonds based on shared electrons; the term is recorded from 1919.
items.cn: covalent 与 covalence 于 20 世纪初被造出，当时化学家需要一个词来指以共享电子为基础的键；该词自 1919 年有记录。

items.en: First date uncertain: the coinage belongs to the early twentieth century, but the earliest printed use is not fully settled, so the date given is approximate.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：这个新造词属于 20 世纪初，但最早的印刷用例尚无完全定论，因此给出的年代只是约数。

note.en: The first group shares the valere stem and is easily mixed up; the second group names the other bond types and the qualities used to contrast them.
note.cn: 第一组共享 valere 词干，极易混淆；第二组是其他键型以及用于对照的性质。

entries.definition: The noun for the sharing itself; covalent is the adjective that describes a bond of this kind.
entries.definitionCN: 指「共享」这一性质的名词；covalent 是描述这类键的形容词。

entries.definition: The combining capacity of an atom, a number; sharing electrons is one way of satisfying it, not the same thing.
entries.definitionCN: 指原子的化合能力，是一个数；共享电子是满足它的一种方式，并不等同。

entries.definition: The British variant of valence; it is a count, while covalent describes the kind of link.
entries.definitionCN: valence 的英式变体；它是计数，而 covalent 描述连接种类。

entries.definition: Also from valere, but it describes bravery rather than combining power; the shared root does not make it a chemistry word.
entries.definitionCN: 同样出自 valere，但描述勇敢而非化合能力；共享词根并不使它成为化学词。

entries.definition: Describing bonds made by electron transfer and electrostatic attraction, the usual opposite of covalent in teaching.
entries.definitionCN: 描述由电子转移与静电吸引形成的键，在教学中通常是 covalent 的对照项。

entries.definition: Describing the shared-electron sea of metals, a third arrangement beside covalent and ionic.
entries.definitionCN: 描述金属共享电子海的结构，是与共价、离子并列的第三种安排。

entries.definition: Describing a covalent bond whose electrons are shared unequally; it is a variety of covalent, not its opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 描述电子共享不均的共价键；它是共价的一种，而非其反面。

entries.definition: Describing matter made of molecules, which covalent bonds commonly build; it names the product, not the link.
entries.definitionCN: 描述由分子构成的物质，共价键常构成这类物质；它命名产物，而非连接。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb, the real prefix pattern and real laboratory phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、真实的前缀同化模式与真实的实验室说法。

normal.en: Co- together plus valent strength: two atoms hold the bond jointly, each contributing an electron.
normal.cn: co-「共同」加 valent「力量」：两个原子共同持有这条键，各自出一个电子。

normal.en: The family runs covalent, covalence, covalently, valence and valency.
normal.cn: 同族词有 covalent、covalence、covalently、valence 与 valency。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the applications: covalent bond, covalent crystal, covalent modification.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出应用：共价键、共价晶体、共价修饰。

normal.en: Co- is the assimilated form of com-, the same prefix heard in cooperate and connect.
normal.cn: co- 是 com- 的同化形式，与 cooperate、connect 中的前缀相同。

normal.en: Covalent and ionic are taught as a pair: sharing against transferring.
normal.cn: covalent 与 ionic 总成对教授：共享对转移。

abstract.en: Picture two hands on one rope, neither letting go.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手握着同一根绳，谁都不松。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of dancers who own the same step between them.
abstract.cn: 想象一对舞者，彼此之间共有同一个舞步。

abstract.en: Picture a fence whose two owners both pay for the same post.
abstract.cn: 想象一道篱笆，两户人家都为同一根柱子出钱。

examples.en: Water molecules are held together by polar covalent bonds.
examples.cn: 水分子由极性共价键维系在一起。

examples.en: The two elements form a covalent compound rather than a salt.
examples.cn: 这两种元素形成共价化合物，而不是盐。

examples.en: Enzymes often make a temporary covalent intermediate.
examples.cn: 酶常常形成暂时的共价中间体。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「co（共同）+ valent（力量）」——两边共同出力握住同一条键 → 共价的

root: 拉丁 valere「有力量、有价值」→ valens「有力量的」→ valentia「力量、容量」→ 英语 valence「化合价」；加 com-（同化为 co-「共同」）→ 20 世纪初造出 covalent「共价的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one arrangement: two atoms hold the same electrons between them. The arrangement then names a compound, a radius, a crystal, a biochemical attachment, a catalytic trick, a cross-link and finally the degree of sharing inside an ionic bond.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种安排展开：两个原子在彼此之间共同持有同一对电子。这种安排随后命名一种化合物、一种半径、一种晶体、一种生化连接、一种催化手法、一种交联，最后是离子键内部的共享程度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands gripping the middle of one rope, so that neither holds it alone.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手各握住一根绳的中段，谁也不是独自持有。

branches.en: THE SHARING ITSELF: one pair of electrons belongs to two atoms at once.
branches.cn: 共享本身：一对电子同时属于两个原子。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: a whole compound built by such sharing, with no ions.
branches.cn: 物质：由这种共享构成、不含离子的整个化合物。

branches.en: MEASURE AND REPEAT: half a bond length becomes a radius, and a repeated bond becomes a crystal.
branches.cn: 测量与重复：半个键长成为半径，重复的键成为晶体。

branches.en: PERMANENT ATTACHMENT: groups fixed onto molecules, and chains locked into a network.
branches.cn: 永久连接：基团被固定到分子上，链被锁进网络。

branches.en: MECHANISM AND DEGREE: a temporary bond used by an enzyme, and how much sharing an ionic bond really has.
branches.cn: 机理与程度：酶所用的暂时键，以及离子键实际的共享程度。

intro.en: Covalent is a textbook modern compound: a Latin prefix, a Latin participle stem and an English ending, all transparent.
intro.cn: covalent 是教科书式的现代复合词：拉丁前缀、拉丁分词词干与英语词尾，全都透明可读。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere and valens supply the stem, and com- supplies the prefix; no single Latin word covalent exists, because the compound was made in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 valere 与 valens 提供词干，com- 提供前缀；拉丁语中并不存在 covalent 这一单词，因为它是英语造的复合词。

items.example: The prefix says the two atoms hold the link jointly.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀说明两个原子共同持有这条键。

items.structure: valere, valui, valitum (Latin verb, second conjugation)
items.example: The verb supplies the idea of capacity or worth.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「容量、价值」的意思。

items.example: The participle is the source of the -valent ending.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词是 -valent 词尾的来源。

items.example: The noun became the chemical term for combining capacity.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词成了表示化合能力的化学术语。

items.structure: valentia through French and German chemistry
items.example: Carbon has a valence of four in most compounds.
items.exampleCN: 碳在多数化合物中化合价为四。

items.example: A covalent bond holds the two hydrogen atoms together.
items.exampleCN: 一条共价键把两个氢原子结合在一起。

items.example: Covalence is the noun behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: covalence 是形容词背后的名词。

items.example: The drug is covalently attached to the protein.
items.exampleCN: 这种药以共价方式接到蛋白质上。

items.example: Valency is counted in bonds, not in electrons alone.
items.exampleCN: 化合价按键计数，而不只是按电子计数。

items.example: Ionic and covalent bonds are taught as two extremes.
items.exampleCN: 离子键与共价键被当作两个极端来教。

definition_zh: 雕塑家；雕刻家；塑造者
definition_en: a person who makes sculpture, whether by carving, modelling or casting
core_image: 一块巨石立在工坊中央，人绕着它走，手上全是石粉，像在与石头对话
scene: 采石场的粉尘落在围裙上，一位工匠把凿子抵住石面， The sculptor worked the block from every side before shaping a face.
sceneCN: 这里 sculptor 指「以雕刻方式创作雕塑的人」（第 1 个义项：石雕者）；句意为那位雕塑家从各个方向处理石块，然后才雕出面孔。图中可辨识物件：石块、凿子、木槌、围裙上的石粉与转台。

senses.title: A carver of stone
senses.definition: a person who cuts or carves stone into a form
senses.definitionCN: 把石材切凿成形体的人
senses.example: The sculptor spent a year removing surplus marble from the block.
senses.exampleCN: 这位雕塑家花了一年时间，把多余的大理石从石块上凿去。
senses.why: Latin sculptor was an agent noun from sculpere 'to carve', so the word first points to cutting rather than to modelling.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 sculptor 是由 sculpere「雕刻」构成的施动名词，所以这个词最初指向切凿，而不是塑形。

senses.title: A modeller in clay or wax
senses.definition: a person who builds up forms in a soft material instead of cutting them away
senses.definitionCN: 以软质材料层层堆加形体、而非削减材料的人
senses.example: Working as a sculptor in clay, she built the figure up in coils.
senses.exampleCN: 她以黏土雕塑为业，用泥条把人物一圈圈堆起来。
senses.why: The craft widened from carving to adding material, and the agent noun followed the maker rather than the method.
senses.whyCN: 这门手艺从削减材料扩展到堆加材料，施动名词跟随的是制作者，而不是方法。

senses.title: One who casts in bronze
senses.definition: a person who makes sculpture by casting molten metal in a mould
senses.definitionCN: 把熔化的金属浇入模具以制作雕塑的人
senses.example: The sculptor prepared a wax model before the foundry cast it in bronze.
senses.exampleCN: 雕塑家先做好蜡模，再由铸造工坊浇铸成青铜。
senses.why: Casting is a separate workshop stage, yet the finished figure is still credited to the sculptor who designed it.
senses.whyCN: 浇铸是另一个工坊环节，但完成的雕像仍归功于设计它的雕塑家。

senses.title: A professional working on commission
senses.titleCN: 接受委托的职业雕塑者
senses.definition: a sculptor who makes work to order for a public body, a church or a collector
senses.definitionCN: 为公共机构、教堂或收藏者按订单创作的雕塑家
senses.example: The cathedral commissioned a sculptor from Florence for the tomb.
senses.exampleCN: 主教座堂为这座陵墓委托了一位佛罗伦萨雕塑家。
senses.why: Once patrons paid for work in advance, the word named a recognised profession rather than any skilled carver.
senses.whyCN: 当委托人预先付费，这个词便指一种被认可的职业，而不是任何熟练的凿石者。

senses.title: An artist ranked beside painters
senses.titleCN: 与画家并列的造型艺术家
senses.definition: a maker of three-dimensional art recognised as one of the fine arts
senses.definitionCN: 被承认属于美术门类的三维艺术创作者
senses.example: The exhibition pairs each painter with a sculptor of the same decade.
senses.exampleCN: 展览为每位画家配一位同年代的雕塑家。
senses.why: In the academy system sculpture took its place beside painting, and the person practising it needed a title of equal standing.
senses.whyCN: 在学院体系中，雕塑与绘画并列，从事雕塑的人也需要一个地位相当的头衔。

senses.title: A figure identified with a period or school
senses.titleCN: 代表某一时期或流派的雕塑者
senses.definition: a sculptor whose manner defines a style, usually named with a period
senses.definitionCN: 手法足以界定一种风格、常与时期连称的雕塑家
senses.example: Scholars describe the doorway as the work of a Romanesque sculptor.
senses.exampleCN: 学者把这个门廊描述为一位罗曼式雕塑家的作品。
senses.why: Style history groups anonymous makers under schools, so the word attaches to periods as well as to named individuals.
senses.whyCN: 风格史把佚名制作者归入流派，因此这个词既系于个人，也系于时期。

senses.title: The maker of one named work
senses.titleCN: 某件具体作品的创作者
senses.definition: the particular person credited with a single monument or figure
senses.definitionCN: 被记在某座纪念碑或某尊造像名下的具体个人
senses.example: The plaque names the sculptor of the fountain but not its engineer.
senses.exampleCN: 铭牌写着喷泉的雕塑者，却没有写工程师。
senses.why: Attribution turns a general role into a credit line, so the word can point to one person behind one object.
senses.whyCN: 归属把一般身份变成一行署名，因此这个词可以指一件作品背后的那个人。

senses.title: One who shapes something abstract
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：塑造抽象之物的力量
senses.definition: figuratively, a person or force that gives form to something without carving it
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法：不靠雕刻而赋予某物形体的个人或力量
senses.example: Time is the sculptor of coastlines, wearing cliffs into arches.
senses.exampleCN: 时间是海岸线的雕塑家，把悬崖磨成拱门。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps only the shaping and drops the chisel, so anything that gives form can be called its sculptor.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻只保留塑形，丢掉了凿子，因此凡是赋予形体者都可称为它的雕塑家。

intro.en: Sculptor comes directly from Latin sculptor, an agent noun built on sculpere 'to carve'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: sculptor 直接来自拉丁 sculptor，它是由 sculpere「雕刻」构成的施动名词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sculpere meant 'to carve, cut, chisel'. Source uncertain: its deeper origin is not established, so any root proposed for it is a reconstruction rather than a witnessed form.
items.cn: sculpere 意为「雕刻、切凿、镌刻」。来源不确定：其更深的来源并无定论，凡为其提出的词根均属重构形式，而非实际书证。

items.en: The agent suffix -or, added to the stem sculpt-, produced sculptor, 'the one who carves'.
items.cn: 施动后缀 -or 加在词干 sculpt- 上，构成 sculptor，即「雕刻的人」。

items.en: Sculptura named both the act of carving and the carved object, and it became the parent of English sculpture.
items.cn: sculptura 既指雕刻的行为，也指雕成的物件，后来成为英语「雕塑」一词的来源。

items.en: English took sculptor from Latin in the sixteenth century, at the same time as sculpture, as a learned term for the art.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪从拉丁语借入 sculptor，与表示「雕塑」的名词同时进入，作为这门艺术的学术用语。

items.en: Older English said carver for the worker; sculptor entered as the dignified word for the same trade and slowly displaced it in art contexts.
items.cn: 较早的英语用「雕刻匠」指这名工匠；sculptor 作为同一行当的正式称谓进入，并逐渐在艺术语境中取代了前者。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the word settled as the standard title for a maker of sculpture, and later art history extended it to anonymous makers of a period.
items.cn: 自十八世纪起，这个词固定为雕塑制作者的标准称谓，后来艺术史又把它扩展到某一时期的佚名制作者。

note.en: The first group holds forms of the same word family that are often confused with sculptor; the second holds words for people who make three-dimensional work by different methods.
note.cn: 第一组是常与 sculptor 混淆的同族词形；第二组是按不同方法制作三维作品的人。

entries.definition: The art or the object produced; sculptor is the person, sculpture is the thing or the activity.
entries.definitionCN: 指这门艺术或雕成的物件；sculptor 是人，sculpture 是物或活动。

entries.definition: Having the qualities of sculpture, especially solid form and modelled surfaces.
entries.definitionCN: 具有雕塑特质的，尤其指坚实的形体与塑出的表面。

entries.definition: To make by carving or shaping, a verb formed from sculpture in English.
entries.definitionCN: 通过雕刻或塑形来制作，是英语中由 sculpture 逆构出的动词。

entries.definition: One who cuts wood, stone or ivory; the word stresses the knife or chisel rather than the finished art.
entries.definitionCN: 切凿木材、石材或象牙的人；强调刀凿，而非完成的艺术品。

entries.definition: One who shapes soft material such as clay or wax into a form, building up rather than cutting away.
entries.definitionCN: 把黏土或蜡等软质材料塑成形体的人，以堆加而非削减方式工作。

entries.definition: One who melts and casts metal in a mould; the founder executes what the sculptor designed.
entries.definitionCN: 熔化金属并浇入模具的人；铸造者实现雕塑家的设计。

entries.definition: A maker of art in any medium; sculptor is the narrower title for one working in three dimensions.
entries.definitionCN: 以任何媒介创作艺术的人；sculptor 是专指三维创作者的较窄称谓。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin stem, the real suffix and the actual workshop stages behind the word.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词干、真实的后缀，以及这个词背后真实的工坊环节。

normal.en: Sculpere 'to carve' plus -or 'one who' gives the carver, the person behind the chisel.
normal.cn: sculpere「雕刻」加 -or「做……的人」，就是拿凿子的人。

normal.en: Actor, doctor and sculptor all end in -or, each naming a person by what they do.
normal.cn: 「演员」「医生」与「雕塑家」都以同一个表示施动者的词尾收尾，都按所做的事来指人。

normal.en: A sculptor does not add paint; the material itself is the form.
normal.cn: 雕塑家不靠颜料，材料本身就是形体。

normal.en: The same person may carve stone, model clay and approve a bronze cast.
normal.cn: 同一个人可能凿石、塑泥，还要审定青铜浇铸。

normal.en: A plaque usually names the sculptor before it names the engineer.
normal.cn: 铭牌上通常先出现雕塑家，再出现工程师。

abstract.en: Picture a block with a figure already inside it, waiting to be let out.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头里早已藏着一个人形，等着被放出来。

abstract.en: Picture hands that trust the stone more than they trust their own plan.
abstract.cn: 想象一双手信任石头，胜过信任自己的图稿。

abstract.en: Picture a face that exists in three dimensions and changes with every step you take.
abstract.cn: 想象一张存在于三维中的脸，随你每一步移动而改变。

examples.en: The city invited a sculptor to design the memorial for the harbour.
examples.cn: 这座城市邀请一位雕塑家为港口设计纪念碑。

examples.en: As a sculptor, he preferred wax models to drawings.
examples.cn: 作为雕塑家，他更偏爱蜡模而非草图。

examples.en: The sculptor signed the base of the figure with a small chisel mark.
examples.cn: 雕塑家在小像底座留下一个小小的凿痕作为签名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 sculptor 拆成 sculpt「雕刻」加 or「做……的人」——雕刻的人就是雕塑家；谐音近「石可破它」，凿子能破开石头，破石的人正是这行工匠。

root: 拉丁 sculpere「雕刻、切凿」加施动后缀 -or 构成 sculptor「雕刻的人」，英语于十六世纪直接借入；同源的 sculptura 演变为英语「雕塑」一词。sculpere 的更深来源无定论，相关词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the stone carver, then move to the clay modeller, the bronze caster, the commissioned professional, the fine-arts artist, the period style, the credited maker of one work and finally a shaping force in metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从凿石者出发，依次扩展到塑泥者、铸铜者、受委托的职业者、与绘画并列的造型艺术家、时期风格、某件作品的署名者，最后是比喻中的塑形力量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person who removes material until a form appears, standing between a raw block and a finished figure.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人不断削去材料，直到形体出现，站在原石与成品之间。

branches.en: THE CARVER: the root meaning is the person who cuts stone, with the chisel as the defining tool.
branches.cn: 凿刻者：核心含义是切凿石材的人，凿子是其标志性工具。

branches.en: OTHER METHODS: the same maker can build up soft material or send a model to the foundry for casting.
branches.cn: 其他方法：同一位制作者可以堆加软质材料，也可以把模子交给工坊浇铸。

branches.en: SOCIAL STANDING: the word moves from a paid craftsman under contract to an artist ranked with painters.
branches.cn: 社会地位：这个词从按合约取酬的工匠，上升到与画家并列的艺术家。

branches.en: THE NAME ON THE WORK: style history ties the maker to a period, and attribution ties one person to one monument.
branches.cn: 作品上的名字：风格史把制作者系于时期，归属则把某个人系于某座纪念碑。

branches.en: WITHOUT A CHISEL: the final sense keeps only the act of giving form, so time or weather can be the sculptor.
branches.cn: 没有凿子：最后一个义项只保留赋予形体的动作，于是时间或风雨也能成为雕塑家。

intro.en: Sculptor is transparent: a Latin verb stem, an agent suffix, and a small English family built on it.
intro.cn: sculptor 结构透明：一个拉丁动词词干、一个施动后缀，以及在其上构成的一小族英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin sculpere 'to carve' yields sculptor 'carver' and sculptura 'carving'; English borrowed both and later added sculpt and sculptural.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sculpere「雕刻」衍生 sculptor「雕刻者」与 sculptura「雕刻」；英语把两者借入，后来又添上表示雕刻的动词与形容词。

items.structure: sculpere, sculpo, sculpsi (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The verb names the physical act behind every sense of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词命名了这个词所有义项背后的具体动作。

items.example: The suffix marks the person rather than the activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记的是人，而不是活动。

items.example: Latin used the noun for the person who cut stone or wood.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语用这个名词指切凿石头或木头的人。

items.meaning: the act or product of an action
items.example: The suffix turns a verb of making into a name for the made thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把制作动词转为制成之物的名称。

items.example: The noun covered both the process and its result.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时涵盖过程与结果。

items.example: English later shortened the noun into a working verb.
items.exampleCN: 英语后来把名词缩短成可用的动词。

items.meaning: the art or an object made in three dimensions
items.meaningCN: 三维造型艺术或其作品
items.example: The noun names both the practice and what it produces.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词既指这门实践，也指其产物。

items.example: The adjective describes solid, modelled qualities in any medium.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述任何媒介中坚实、有塑造感的特质。

derivatives.structure: sculptor + -ess (feminine agent suffix, from Old French -esse, Latin -issa)
derivatives.meaning: a woman who makes sculpture, an older marked form now little used
derivatives.meaningCN: 女性雕塑家，带性别标记的旧式说法，今已少用

derivatives.meaning: having the three-dimensional quality of sculpture rather than of painting
derivatives.meaningCN: 具有雕塑般三维质感而非绘画质感的

definition_zh: 与……相比；把两者放在同一标准上衡量，以看出高低或异同
definition_en: used when two things are weighed on the same scale in order to show how they differ in amount, quality or level
core_image: 两块厚薄不同的布样并排摆在同一条刻度尺上，指针各停在一格
scene: 质检台上两块布样并排压在同一条刻度尺下，指针各停在一格。 In comparison with last year's fabric, this year's is slightly thinner.
sceneCN: 这里指把今年与去年的布料放在同一标准上量（第 1 个义项：与……相比）；句意为与去年的布料相比，今年的略薄一些。图中可辨识物件：布样、刻度尺、指针。

collocations.phrase: in comparison with the previous year
in comparison with the standard model

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「配对、等同」动词经法语而来，义为「比较」
由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「比较」
由该名词加「可……的」形容词尾构成，义为「可比的」
由该词干加表示关系的形容词尾构成，义为「比较的；比较级」
由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「同样地」
由否定前缀加形容词构成，义为「无可比拟的」

senses.title: Weighing two like things
senses.titleCN: 把同类事物放在同一标准上比
senses.definition: used to set two comparable things on one scale
senses.definitionCN: 把两个可比的对象放在同一个衡量标准上
senses.example: In comparison with the earlier model, the new engine uses far less fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 与早先的型号相比，新发动机耗油少得多。
senses.why: The phrase assumes a shared measure; that is why the two items must belong to the same class.
senses.whyCN: 这一短语预设存在共同的衡量标准，因此两个对象必须属于同一类别。

senses.title: The fronted frame
senses.definition: placed at the front of a clause to name the benchmark before making the point
senses.definitionCN: 置于从句开头，先说基准，再给出结论
senses.example: In comparison with earlier estimates, the final figure looks modest.
senses.exampleCN: 与早先的估计相比，最终数字显得温和。
senses.why: Fronting the phrase tells the reader which item is the yardstick before the judgement arrives.
senses.whyCN: 把它提到句首，读者先知道哪一项是尺子，再收到判断。

senses.title: Statistical comparison
senses.definition: used when two sets of figures are set side by side
senses.definitionCN: 把两组数字并置时使用
senses.example: In comparison with the 2018 figures, the 2024 figures rose by a fifth.
senses.exampleCN: 与 2018 年的数字相比，2024 年的数字上升了五分之一。
senses.why: Numbers need a declared baseline, and this phrase supplies it in one stroke.
senses.whyCN: 数字需要明确的基准，这个短语一笔就交代清楚。

senses.title: Benchmarking against a standard
senses.definition: used in quality work to measure a product against an agreed standard
senses.definitionCN: 在质量管理中把产品与约定标准对照
senses.example: In comparison with the industry standard, the sample failed on two measures.
senses.exampleCN: 与行业标准相比，该样品在两项指标上不合格。
senses.why: Here the second item is not a rival product but a fixed yardstick, so the phrase measures compliance rather than preference.
senses.whyCN: 这里的第二项不是竞争产品而是固定标尺，因此衡量的是合规而非喜好。

senses.title: Academic group comparison
senses.definition: used in research writing to contrast an experimental group with a baseline group
senses.definitionCN: 在研究写作中把实验组与基线组并置
senses.example: In comparison with the baseline group, the trained group recalled more words.
senses.exampleCN: 与基线组相比，受训组回忆出的单词更多。
senses.why: Research prose needs the baseline named explicitly, and this frame keeps the two groups in one sentence.
senses.whyCN: 研究写作需要明确点出基线，这一框架把两组放进同一句。

senses.title: A relative judgement
senses.definition: used to judge one thing as better, worse or larger than another
senses.definitionCN: 判断一物比另一物更好、更差或更大
senses.example: In comparison with the older treatment, the new one is both cheaper and safer.
senses.exampleCN: 与旧疗法相比，新疗法既便宜又安全。
senses.why: The phrase licenses a comparative adjective in the main clause, because a scale has already been set.
senses.whyCN: 短语为主句里的比较级形容词提供依据，因为尺度已经立好。

senses.title: A share of the whole
senses.definition: used to set a part against the total it belongs to
senses.definitionCN: 把部分与它所属的整体对照
senses.example: In comparison with the whole budget, the research share is tiny.
senses.exampleCN: 与整个预算相比，研究所占的份额很小。
senses.why: A part-to-whole ratio is still a comparison, but the second term is the container rather than a rival.
senses.whyCN: 部分与整体的比率仍是比较，只是第二项是容器而非对手。

senses.title: Comparison, not opposition
senses.definition: used to measure degree on a shared scale, where in contrast to would mark opposition
senses.definitionCN: 在同一尺度上衡量程度，而「与……形成对照」则标示对立
senses.example: In comparison with the northern route, the southern route is merely longer.
senses.exampleCN: 与北线相比，南线只是更长一些。
senses.why: The two phrases divide the work: comparison weighs, contrast opposes, and mixing them blurts the point.
senses.whyCN: 两个短语分工：比较负责称量，对照负责对立，混用会让重点含糊。

intro.en: Comparison comes from Latin comparatio, built on comparare, to pair or match, itself from com-, together, and par, equal. The noun passed through Old French into English; the prepositional phrase is later and its first date is approximate.
intro.cn: comparison 源自拉丁语 comparatio，出自动词 comparare「配对、使相等」，后者由 com-「一起」与 par「相等」构成。名词经古法语进入英语；介词短语更晚，首见年代为约数。

items.en: Par means equal and also gives parity and peer in English.
items.cn: par 意为「相等」，也给出英语的 parity 与 peer。

items.en: Com- means together, so the verb pictures two things placed side by side.
items.cn: com- 意为「一起」，动词便画出两物并排的画面。

items.en: Comparare means to pair, match or bring together for weighing.
items.cn: comparare 意为「配对、使相配、放在一起称量」。

items.en: The noun names the act of setting two things on one scale.
items.cn: 名词指把两物放在同一尺度上的行为。

items.en: The word entered English through Old French comparaison in the Middle English period.
items.cn: 该词经古法语 comparaison 于中古英语时期进入英语。

items.en: The frame in comparison with belongs to modern written English; its exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 这一介词框架属近代书面英语，确切首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group occupies the same slot and can be mistaken for this phrase; the second group holds other ways of naming a yardstick.
note.cn: 第一组占同一位置，容易被误认作本短语；第二组是其他点出标尺的说法。

entries.definition: To and with are interchangeable here, with with slightly more common in British writing.
entries.definitionCN: 两个介词在此可互换，其中 with 在英式写作里略常见。

entries.definition: It stresses that two things are opposite rather than merely different in degree.
entries.definitionCN: 它强调两物相反，而不只是程度不同。

entries.definition: The participle drops the noun and works as a leaner opener.
entries.definitionCN: 分词形式省去名词，作更精简的开头。

entries.definition: It stands alone between clauses and takes no benchmark after it.
entries.definitionCN: 它独立用于句间，后面不带基准。

entries.definition: It sets a value against a base, often in technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 它把数值放在基准之上，多用于技术写作。

entries.definition: In charts, against introduces the standard that the data are plotted on.
entries.definitionCN: 在图表中，它引出数据所依据的基准。

entries.definition: It pictures two items placed next to each other for the eye to judge.
entries.definitionCN: 它画出两物并排放置、由眼睛判断的画面。

entries.definition: It sets two parties or options against each other, often in disputes.
entries.definitionCN: 它把两方或两个选项对立起来，多用于争执。

normalIntro.en: The normal associations use the real Latin pair, the real prepositions and the comparison-contrast division of labour.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实拉丁语对、真实介词以及比较与对照的分工。

normal.en: Par means equal, so comparison first makes the two items level.
normal.cn: par 意为「相等」，比较先要把两项摆平。

normal.en: Com- means together, so the phrase always needs a second item.
normal.cn: com- 意为「一起」，短语总要有第二项。

normal.en: With and to both work; with is the safer choice in British prose.
normal.cn: 两个介词都可用，英式文字里 with 更稳妥。

normal.en: Comparison weighs degree; contrast declares opposition.
normal.cn: 比较称量程度，对照宣告对立。

normal.en: The benchmark may be a rival, a standard or the whole that contains the part.
normal.cn: 基准可以是对手、标准，也可以是包含部分的整体。

abstract.en: Like two cloth samples pressed under one ruler, each pointer stopping at its own mark.
abstract.cn: 像两块布样压在同一把尺下，指针各停一格。

abstract.en: Like a balance beam with two pans, the reading only exists because both are loaded.
abstract.cn: 像两端都放了砝码的天平，读数因两边同时受载才存在。

abstract.en: Like a map scale bar: the distance means nothing until the bar is laid beside it.
abstract.cn: 像地图上的比例尺，不放上去距离就没有意义。

examples.en: In comparison with the 2019 survey, the 2024 survey found fewer first-time buyers.
examples.cn: 与 2019 年的调查相比，2024 年的调查发现首次购房者更少。

examples.en: In comparison with the control group, the treated group recovered faster.
examples.cn: 与对照组相比，治疗组恢复得更快。

examples.en: In comparison with the whole budget, training costs remain small.
examples.cn: 与整个预算相比，培训费用仍然很小。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「因 康帕瑞森 维兹」——两块布样压在同一把尺下，指针各停一格：与……相比

root: comparison 源自拉丁语 comparatio，出自动词 comparare，由表示「一起」的前缀与 par「相等」构成；该介词框架属近代书面英语，首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split by the role of the second item: a like rival, a fronted benchmark, two data sets, an industry standard, a control group, a comparative judgement, a part-to-whole ratio, and the comparison-versus-contrast division.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项按第二项的角色区分：同类对手、前置基准、两组数据、行业标准、对照组、优劣判断、部分与整体、比较与对照的分工。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two cloth samples pressed under one ruler, each pointer stopping at its own mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：两块布样压在同一把尺下，指针各停一格。

branches.en: THE SHARED SCALE: two like things are levelled before any judgement is made.
branches.cn: 共同尺度：两个同类先被摆平，再作判断。

branches.en: THE TWO GROUPS: figures and control groups need a named baseline.
branches.cn: 两组对象：数字与对照组都需要点明基准。

branches.en: THE STANDARD: the second item is a fixed rule, so the reading measures compliance.
branches.cn: 标准：第二项是固定规则，读数衡量的是合规。

branches.en: THE VERDICT: a comparative adjective follows because the scale is already set.
branches.cn: 判断：尺度既定，比较级形容词才随之出现。

branches.en: THE CONTAINER AND THE CONTRAST: part against whole, comparison against opposition.
branches.cn: 容器与对立：部分对整体，比较对对立的划分。

intro.en: The Latin core is par, equal, with com-, together; comparare and comparatio supply the English family.
intro.cn: 拉丁核心是 par「相等」加 com-「一起」；comparare 与 comparatio 提供英语同族词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin elements are par, equal, and com-, together; the verb comparare joins them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁成分是 par「相等」与 com-「一起」，动词 comparare 由两者合成。

items.example: Par also survives in English as a golf and finance term.
items.exampleCN: 这个词在英语里还活用于高尔夫与金融术语。

items.example: The prefix makes the act a joint one.
items.exampleCN: 前缀让这个动作成为共同行为。

items.example: The verb supplies the whole English family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供整族英语词。

items.example: The noun names the act, not the result.

items.meaning: the act or result of comparing
items.example: The noun fills the middle of the fixed phrase.
items.exampleCN: 名词占据固定短语的中间位置。

items.example: The verb is the plain form behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: 动词是名词背后的朴素形式。

items.example: The suffix marks capacity, not achievement.
items.exampleCN: 后缀标记能力，而非已完成。

items.example: Grammar uses the term for the -er form.
items.exampleCN: 语法学用这个词指比较级形式。

latinEntries.structure: comparare, comparo, comparavi, comparatum (verb, first conjugation)

definition_zh: 腹部；腹腔；（昆虫、甲壳类的）腹部
definition_en: the part of the body between the chest and the pelvis, or the rear section of an insect's or crustacean's body
core_image: 躯干中段那个装着肠胃的柔软腔体
scene: 医生先让病人平躺，再轻轻按压腹部寻找痛点。 The surgeon pressed gently on her abdomen to locate the source of the pain.
sceneCN: 这里 abdomen 是「腹部」（第 1 个义项：人体胸部与骨盆之间的区域）；句意为外科医生轻按她的腹部，寻找疼痛的来源。

pos.zh: 昆虫或甲壳动物的腹部体段

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「腹部的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「在腹部；按腹部方式」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「大腹的；肥胖的」
由本词与表示「成形术」的成分构成，义为「腹壁整形术」

senses.title: The human belly region
senses.definition: the front part of the body between the chest and the hips, containing the stomach and intestines
senses.definitionCN: 人体胸部与髋部之间的前部区域，内有胃与肠
senses.example: He felt a sharp pain in his abdomen after dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭后他感到腹部一阵剧痛。
senses.why: Latin abdomen named the belly as a whole; the word entered medical English as the neutral term for the region that holds the digestive organs.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abdomen 整体指「肚子」；这个词作为中性术语进入医学英语，指容纳消化器官的区域。

senses.title: The abdominal cavity
senses.definition: the space inside the body that contains the stomach, intestines, liver, and other organs
senses.definitionCN: 体内容纳胃、肠、肝等器官的空间
senses.example: The scan showed fluid in the abdomen.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示腹腔内有积液。
senses.why: Once the outer belly is named, the same word is extended inward to the cavity behind it.
senses.whyCN: 外部腹部有了名称之后，同一个词又被向内延伸到它后面的腔体。

senses.title: The insect abdomen
senses.definition: the third and rear section of an insect's body, behind the thorax
senses.definitionCN: 昆虫身体第三节，位于胸部之后
senses.example: The wasp's sting sits at the tip of its abdomen.
senses.exampleCN: 黄蜂的刺长在腹部的末端。
senses.why: Entomology borrowed the human term for the rear body segment because it also holds the gut.
senses.whyCN: 昆虫学借用了人体术语来指后部体段，因为那里同样容纳肠道。

senses.title: The crustacean abdomen
senses.definition: the segmented rear part of a crustacean such as a shrimp or crab
senses.definitionCN: 虾或蟹等甲壳动物分节的躯干后部
senses.example: The shrimp flexed its abdomen to propel itself backward.
senses.exampleCN: 虾弯曲腹部，把自己向后推。
senses.why: In arthropods the same body plan repeats, so the belly word naturally covers the tail-like rear section.
senses.whyCN: 节肢动物的身体结构彼此相似，因此这个「肚子」的词自然也能指像尾巴一样的后段。

senses.title: The arachnid abdomen
senses.definition: the rear body part of a spider or similar animal, which contains the digestive and reproductive organs
senses.definitionCN: 蜘蛛等动物躯干的后部，内含消化与生殖器官
senses.example: The spider's abdomen is often larger than its front body.
senses.exampleCN: 蜘蛛的腹部往往比前体更大。
senses.why: The term is a general anatomical label for the hind body, whatever the species.
senses.whyCN: 这个术语是所有物种后部躯体的通用解剖标签。

senses.title: A paunch
senses.definition: a rounded or fat belly, used in everyday speech
senses.definitionCN: 日常口语中指圆鼓或肥胖的肚子
senses.example: He patted his abdomen and laughed about his diet.
senses.exampleCN: 他拍拍自己的肚腩，笑谈起节食。
senses.why: The neutral medical word is softened into a friendly or teasing reference to a large belly.
senses.whyCN: 中性的医学词被软化，用来友善或打趣地指肥大的肚子。

senses.title: Acute abdomen
senses.definition: a medical condition of sudden severe abdominal pain that may need surgery
senses.definitionCN: 突发剧烈腹痛、可能需要手术的医学状况
senses.example: The patient was admitted with an acute abdomen.
senses.exampleCN: 病人因急腹症入院。
senses.why: A body region becomes a clinical label: the abdomen itself signals the emergency.
senses.whyCN: 一个身体区域变成了临床标签：腹部本身就在提示急症。

senses.title: The lower trunk of a vertebrate
senses.definition: the lower trunk region of a vertebrate animal, between the rib cage and the pelvis
senses.definitionCN: 脊椎动物肋骨与骨盆之间的躯干下部区域
senses.example: The frog's abdomen is pale and smooth.
senses.exampleCN: 青蛙的腹部苍白而光滑。
senses.why: Comparative anatomy uses the same term across vertebrates, keeping the meaning close to the original Latin belly.
senses.whyCN: 比较解剖学在各类脊椎动物中沿用同一个词，含义贴近拉丁语原义「肚子」。

intro.en: Abdomen is a Latin anatomical word of uncertain origin; it may be linked to the verb 'to hide', because the belly hides the organs.
intro.cn: abdomen 是一个来源不确定的拉丁语解剖词；它可能与表示「藏起来」的动词有关，因为肚子把器官藏在里面。

items.en: No agreed Indo-European root has been reconstructed for abdomen; the deeper history of the word is source uncertain.
items.cn: abdomen 尚无可公认的原始印欧语词根；这个词更深层的来源不确定。

items.en: Latin abdomen meant 'belly'. One common suggestion links it to abdere 'to hide', but this is a hypothesis, not an established fact.
items.cn: 拉丁语 abdomen 意为「肚子」。一种常见推测把它与 abdere（藏起来）联系起来，但这只是假说，并非定论。

items.en: The adjective abdominalis already existed in Latin medical writing.
items.cn: 形容词 abdominalis 在拉丁医学文献中已经存在。

items.en: French medical texts adopted abdomen in the sixteenth century as a learned term.
items.cn: 十六世纪的法语医学文献把这个词作为学术术语吸收进来。

items.en: English anatomy books took the word from Latin and French, keeping its neutral clinical tone.
items.cn: 英语解剖学著作从拉丁语和法语借入该词，保留了它中性、临床的语气。

items.en: Later biology extended it to insects and crustaceans, whose rear body segment is also called the abdomen.
items.cn: 后来的生物学把它扩展到昆虫与甲壳动物，它们后部的体段同样称作腹部。

note.en: The first group gathers the adjective and related medical forms; the second gathers everyday words for the belly.
note.cn: 第一组收形容词与相关医学形式；第二组收日常表示肚子的词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of or relating to the abdomen'.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「腹部的；与腹部有关的」。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'in the abdomen or by means of the abdomen'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在腹部；以腹部方式」。

entries.definition: An adjective, now rare, meaning 'having a large belly'.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，现已罕见，义为「大腹的；肥胖的」。

entries.definition: Cosmetic surgery that removes excess skin and fat from the abdomen.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「腹壁整形术」，指切除腹部多余皮肤与脂肪的整形手术。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the front of the body below the chest.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「肚子」，是胸部以下身体前部的日常说法。

entries.definition: The organ that receives food, often used loosely for the whole belly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「胃」，也常宽松地指整个腹部。

entries.definition: A child-friendly or informal word for the belly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小肚肚」，是童语或非正式说法。

entries.definition: A large, often protruding belly, especially in an older man.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大肚腩」，尤指年长男性突出的肚子。

entries.definition: The intestines or the belly as a whole, used informally.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，非正式用法，义为「肠子」或整个腹部。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks work from the anatomical collocations and the family of adjectives; the abstract hooks picture the soft middle of the body.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点来自解剖搭配与形容词词族；抽象记忆点想象身体中段那个柔软的腔体。

normal.en: Lower abdomen and upper abdomen divide the belly into two clinical zones.
normal.cn: lower abdomen 与 upper abdomen 把肚子分成两个临床区域。

normal.en: Acute abdomen is the emergency label for sudden severe belly pain.
normal.cn: acute abdomen 是突发剧烈腹痛的急症标签。

normal.en: Abdominal is the adjective, as in abdominal muscles.
normal.cn: 形容词是 abdominal，如 abdominal muscles（腹部肌肉）。

normal.en: Abdominoplasty joins abdomen with the suffix for surgical reshaping.
normal.cn: abdominoplasty 把 abdomen 与表示外科整形的后缀组合起来。

normal.en: Insects and crabs also have an abdomen, because the word names the rear body section.
normal.cn: 昆虫和蟹也有 abdomen，因为这个词指后部体段。

abstract.en: Picture a soft pouch tied around the middle of the body, holding the stomach and intestines.
abstract.cn: 想象身体中段系着一个柔软的袋子，里面装着胃和肠。

abstract.en: Picture an insect drawn as three beads, with the last bead called the abdomen.
abstract.cn: 想象昆虫画成三颗珠子，最后一颗叫腹部。

abstract.en: Picture a doctor's two fingers pressing a patient's belly to find the sore spot.
abstract.cn: 想象医生的两根手指按在病人肚子上，寻找痛点。

examples.en: The pain began in the lower abdomen.
examples.cn: 疼痛从下腹部开始。

examples.en: A bee's abdomen is striped black and yellow.
examples.cn: 蜜蜂的腹部有黑黄条纹。

examples.en: The scan revealed a small mass in his abdomen.
examples.cn: 扫描发现他腹腔里有一个小结节。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布多门」——肚子像一扇门，里面藏着肠胃，门外只看见柔软的腹部。

root: 拉丁语 abdomen（肚子），来源不确定；一种推测与 abdere（藏起来）有关，因为腹部把内脏藏在其后

sensesIntro.en: The senses start with the human belly and its inner cavity, then spread to insects, crustaceans, and spiders, and finally to everyday and clinical uses.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从人的腹部与腹腔开始，扩展到昆虫、甲壳类与蜘蛛，最后落到日常与临床用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the soft middle chamber that holds the gut
core.cn: 核心意象：装着肠子的柔软中段腔体

branches.en: The human and vertebrate belly, seen from outside or as an inner cavity.
branches.cn: 人与脊椎动物的腹部，可从外部看，也可指内部腔体。

branches.en: The rear body section of arthropods, named by analogy with the gut-holding belly.

definition_zh: 导致；造成；以……为结果（先说原因，再说后果）
definition_en: to cause a particular outcome, with the cause as subject and the outcome after the preposition
core_image: 第一张多米诺骨牌被推倒，后面的牌依次倒下，最后一张压住了终点线
scene: 长桌上排好一串骨牌，第一张被轻轻一推，后面的牌依次倒下。 One careless push can result in the fall of the whole row.
sceneCN: 这里指一次推动导致整排骨牌倒下（第 1 个义项：导致某一结果）；句意为一次不小心的推动就能导致整排倒下。图中可辨识物件：骨牌、长桌、终点线。

pos.zh: 固定搭配：结果为导向的因果表达

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「弹回」动词经法语而来，义为「结果；导致」
由该动词加形容词尾构成，义为「由此产生的；合力」
由该动词加分词尾构成，义为「由此产生的」
同根的反向框架，义为「由……造成」
由名词加形容词构成的复合词，义为「结果导向的」

senses.title: Cause to outcome
senses.definition: used when the subject is the cause and the object is the outcome
senses.definitionCN: 主语是原因，介词后是后果
senses.example: A single missed inspection can result in a recall of the batch.
senses.exampleCN: 漏检一次就可能导致整批产品被召回。
senses.why: The preposition points forward along the arrow, so the sentence runs from cause to effect.
senses.whyCN: 介词沿箭头向前指，句子便从原因走向结果。

senses.title: Damage or accident
senses.definition: used when the outcome is harm, loss or an accident
senses.definitionCN: 后果是伤害、损失或事故时使用
senses.example: Poor wiring can result in a fire.
senses.exampleCN: 布线不当可能造成火灾。
senses.why: With harmful outcomes the phrase often stands beside a warning or a safety rule.
senses.whyCN: 后果有害时，这个短语常与警告或安全规则并置。

senses.title: Experimental reading
senses.definition: used in reports to state what a treatment or condition produced
senses.definitionCN: 在报告中说明某种处理或条件产生了什么
senses.example: The higher dose can result in a faster response.
senses.exampleCN: 较高剂量可带来更快的反应。
senses.why: Research prose uses the frame to keep the manipulated variable in subject position.
senses.whyCN: 研究写作借此把被操纵的变量留在主语位置。

senses.title: A gain or improvement
senses.definition: used when the outcome is a benefit or an advance
senses.definitionCN: 后果是益处或进步时使用
senses.example: Better training can result in fewer accidents.
senses.exampleCN: 更好的培训可以减少事故。
senses.why: The frame is neutral about value, so gains and losses both fit the same slot.
senses.whyCN: 这一框架对价值中性，收益与损失都进同一个位置。

senses.title: A medical outcome
senses.definition: used when a condition produces a symptom or illness
senses.definitionCN: 某种状况引发症状或疾病时使用
senses.example: Long exposure can result in hearing loss.
senses.exampleCN: 长期暴露可能导致听力损失。
senses.why: In medicine the outcome is often a state that develops slowly and cannot be undone.
senses.whyCN: 在医学里结果常是缓慢形成且不可逆的状态。

senses.title: Ending in a consequence
senses.definition: used when an action ends in a penalty, dismissal or ruling
senses.definitionCN: 某行为以处罚、解职或裁决告终时使用
senses.example: Repeated breaches can result in dismissal.
senses.exampleCN: 屡次违规可能导致解雇。
senses.why: Here the outcome is a formal consequence imposed by an authority.
senses.whyCN: 这里的结果是由权威施加的正式后果。

senses.title: Academic causal chain
senses.definition: used to link a variable to a measured outcome in research writing
senses.definitionCN: 在研究写作中把一个变量与测量结果连起来
senses.example: Warmer water can result in the migration of the species.
senses.exampleCN: 水温升高可能导致该物种迁移。
senses.why: The mirror phrase result from reverses the arrow, and the pair marks the direction of causation.
senses.whyCN: 反向框架把箭头倒过来，两者共同标出因果方向。

senses.title: Policy consequences
senses.definition: used when a decision produces effects that appear over time
senses.definitionCN: 某项决定产生随时间显现的影响时使用
senses.example: Short-term subsidies can result in long-term dependence.
senses.exampleCN: 短期补贴可能导致长期依赖。
senses.why: Policy writing uses the frame to trace delayed effects that were not obvious at the start.
senses.whyCN: 政策写作借此追踪起初并不明显的延迟后果。

intro.en: Result comes from Latin resultare, to spring back, from re-, back, and saltare, to leap, a frequentative of salire, to jump. The verb passed through French into English; the phrasal frame with in is modern and its first date is approximate.
intro.cn: result 源自拉丁语 resultare「弹回」，由 re-「回」与 saltare「跳」构成，后者是 salire「跳跃」的反复形式。动词经法语进入英语；带介词的框架属近代，首见年代为约数。

items.en: Salire means to jump and also underlies assault and assail.
items.cn: salire 意为「跳」，也是 assault 与 assail 的根基。

items.en: Saltare is the frequentative, to keep jumping or dance.
items.cn: saltare 是反复形式，意为「不断跳、舞蹈」。

items.en: Resultare means to spring back, the image of something bouncing off a surface.
items.cn: resultare 意为「弹回」，画出某物从表面弹开的画面。

items.en: French resulter shifted the image towards what follows from an action.
items.cn: 法语 resulter 把意象转向「由行为产生的结果」。

items.en: English first used result as a verb, then as a noun for the outcome itself.
items.cn: 英语先用它作动词，再作指结果本身的名词。

items.en: The frame fixes the outcome after the preposition; first dates are approximate.
items.cn: 这一框架把后果固定在介词之后，首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group looks identical but reverses the arrow or changes the particle; the second group holds causal verbs of different strength.
note.cn: 第一组形似但箭头相反或小品词不同；第二组是力度不同的因果动词。

entries.definition: It takes the outcome as subject and the cause after from, the mirror of this phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 它以后果作主语、原因放在介词后，是本短语的镜像。

entries.definition: It pictures a route with steps; result in states the outcome more directly.
entries.definitionCN: 它画出有步骤的路线；本短语更直接地说出结果。

entries.definition: The participle attaches to a clause and explains the outcome of an action.
entries.definitionCN: 分词形式挂在从句上，说明行为的结果。

entries.definition: It asserts causation plainly, with no image of a bouncing object.
entries.definitionCN: 它直白地断言因果，没有弹回物的意象。

entries.definition: It usually implies an agent who intentionally produces the outcome.
entries.definitionCN: 它通常暗示施事者有意造成后果。

entries.definition: It pictures an outcome rising from a source, common in formal prose.
entries.definitionCN: 它画出后果自源头升起，多见于正式文字。

entries.definition: It treats the outcome as something made, often deliberately.
entries.definitionCN: 它把后果当作被制造出来的东西，常带有意为之。

normalIntro.en: The normal associations use the real Latin leap, the arrow direction and the contrasting frame.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁语「跳」、箭头方向与反向框架。

normal.en: The Latin verb meant to spring back, so a result is what bounces out of an action.
normal.cn: 拉丁动词意为「弹回」，结果就是行为弹出来的东西。

normal.en: In this frame the subject is the cause and the object is the outcome.
normal.cn: 此框架里主语是原因，宾语是后果。

normal.en: Its mirror result from puts the outcome first; the two mark the arrow.
normal.cn: 镜像短语把后果放前，两者共同标出箭头。

normal.en: The frame is value-neutral: gains and losses both fit.
normal.cn: 框架对价值中性，收益与损失都能进。

normal.en: Compared with lead to, it states the endpoint more directly.
normal.cn: 与「通向」相比，它更直接地说出终点。

abstract.en: Like the first domino: one push, and the whole row falls in order.
abstract.cn: 像第一张骨牌：一推之下，整排依次倒下。

abstract.en: Like a ball striking a wall and rebounding into the player's hands.
abstract.cn: 像球撞墙弹回，落进球员手里。

abstract.en: Like a stone thrown into a pond, the splash arriving after the throw.
abstract.cn: 像石子投进池塘，水花在抛出之后才到。

examples.en: A delay in parts can result in a week-long shutdown.
examples.cn: 零件延迟可能导致为期一周的停工。

examples.en: Higher humidity can result in slower drying.

examples.en: One missed step can result in a failed audit.

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split by the outcome: a general consequence, damage, an experimental reading, a gain, a disease, a formal penalty, a research chain and a delayed policy effect.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项按后果类别区分：一般后果、损害、实验读数、收益、疾病、正式处罚、研究链条、延迟的政策后果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first domino pushed, the row falling in order to the finish line.
core.cn: 核心意象：第一张骨牌被推倒，整排依次倒向终点线。

branches.en: THE ARROW: cause in subject position, outcome after the preposition.
branches.cn: 箭头：原因占主语位，后果在介词后。

branches.en: THE HARM: fire, hearing loss and failure are outcomes nobody wants.
branches.cn: 损害：火灾、听力损失与失败都是不想要的后果。

branches.en: THE READING: experiments and training report measured gains or speeds.
branches.cn: 读数：实验与培训报告可测量的收益或速度。

branches.en: THE PENALTY: an authority imposes dismissal or a ruling.
branches.cn: 处罚：权威施加解职或裁决。

branches.en: THE DELAYED EFFECT: subsidies produce dependence only later.
branches.cn: 延迟后果：补贴要到后来才造成依赖。

definition_zh: 结构的；结构性的；建筑承重构造的；系统深层的
definition_en: relating to the structure or framework of something, especially to its load-bearing parts or its underlying organization
core_image: 一座桥的钢架剖面被抽掉一块，周围的梁柱仍把重量一步步传向地基
scene: 这里指「结构的」。 The survey found structural damage beneath the bridge deck.
sceneCN: 这里 structural 是「结构上的、承重构造的」（第 2 个义项：与建筑的梁柱和承重体系有关）；句意：检测发现桥面下方存在结构损伤。图中可辨识物件：钢梁、桥墩、裂缝、承重箭头。

pos.zh: 结构的；结构性的；建筑承重构造的；系统深层的

derivatives.zh: 结构主义者；结构主义的

senses.title: Relating to a framework
senses.definition: relating to the way the parts of something are arranged and connected to form a whole
senses.definitionCN: 与某物各部分如何排列、连接成一个整体的方式有关
senses.example: The essay compares the structural features of the two novels.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章比较了这两部小说的结构特征。
senses.why: Latin structura named a fitting together, from struere 'to build'; the adjective therefore points to arrangement rather than to surface appearance.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 structura 指「拼合、建造」，出自 struere「建造」；因此这个形容词指向排列方式，而不是表面外观。

senses.title: Load-bearing parts of a building
senses.definition: relating to the beams, columns, walls and foundations that carry weight and keep a building standing
senses.definitionCN: 与承担重量、使建筑站立的梁、柱、墙与基础有关
senses.example: A structural engineer approved the plans before construction began.
senses.exampleCN: 施工开始前，结构工程师批准了图纸。
senses.why: This engineering sense is the concrete core of the metaphor: the parts that bear load are literally the structure, and damage to them threatens the whole.
senses.whyCN: 这一工程义项是比喻的具体核心：承重的部件就是字面意义上的结构，它们的损伤会威胁整体。

senses.title: Of a language as a system
senses.titleCN: 语言学中的结构：把语言视为系统
senses.definition: in linguistics, describing language as a system of relations among sounds, words and sentences rather than as a list of items
senses.definitionCN: 在语言学中，把语言描述为声音、词与句子之间的关系系统，而不是一份条目清单
senses.example: Structural analysis shows that the two dialects share the same sound system.
senses.exampleCN: 结构分析显示，这两种方言共享同一套语音系统。
senses.why: Twentieth-century linguistics shifted attention from isolated words to the network that holds them together, and structural became the label for that viewpoint.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪语言学把关注点从孤立的词转向维系它们的网络，structural 成为这一视角的标签。

senses.title: Underlying causes in a system
senses.definition: describing a cause that lies in the organization of a system rather than in the choices of one person
senses.definitionCN: 指某项原因存在于系统的组织方式中，而不是某个人的选择中
senses.example: Poverty in the region is structural, not a matter of individual effort.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的贫困是结构性的，与个人努力无关。
senses.why: If the arrangement of institutions produces the outcome, blaming individuals misses the mechanism; structural names that mechanism and is often opposed to personal or accidental.
senses.whyCN: 如果制度安排产生了这一结果，归咎个人就错失了机制；structural 命名这一机制，常与「个人的」「偶然的」相对。

senses.title: Change that alters the framework
senses.titleCN: 改变框架本身的结构性变革
senses.definition: describing reform or change that alters the basic organization of an economy, industry or institution rather than adjusting its surface
senses.definitionCN: 指改变经济、产业或机构基本组织方式的改革，而不是表面调整
senses.example: The country undertook structural reforms in taxation and labour law.
senses.exampleCN: 该国在税制与劳动法方面进行了结构性改革。
senses.why: Policy language distinguishes a structural reform from a temporary fix: the former changes the rules that generate outcomes, not just the outcomes themselves.
senses.whyCN: 政策语言把结构性改革与临时补救区分开：前者改变产生结果的规则，而不只是结果本身。

senses.title: Arrangement of molecules or cells
senses.titleCN: 分子或细胞层面的结构
senses.definition: in chemistry and biology, relating to the arrangement of atoms, molecules or tissues and how that arrangement determines function
senses.definitionCN: 在化学与生物学中，与原子、分子或组织的排列方式以及该排列如何决定功能有关
senses.example: Structural biology revealed how the protein binds its target.
senses.exampleCN: 结构生物学揭示了这种蛋白质如何结合靶点。
senses.why: Function follows form at the molecular scale: knowing how the parts are arranged explains what the molecule can do, which is why the adjective attaches to biology.
senses.whyCN: 在分子尺度上功能随形式而来：了解各部分如何排列，就能解释分子能做什么，因此这个形容词常与生物学搭配。

senses.title: Inequality built into society
senses.titleCN: 制度化的结构性不平等
senses.definition: describing disadvantage that is reproduced by the rules, norms and organization of a society rather than by individual prejudice alone
senses.definitionCN: 指由社会的规则、规范与组织方式不断再生产出来的不利处境，而非仅由个人偏见造成
senses.example: The report documented structural inequality in housing and schooling.
senses.exampleCN: 报告记录了指住房与教育方面的结构性不平等。
senses.why: This social sense extends the engineering image to institutions: the rules act as beams that distribute advantage unevenly, so the pattern persists even when individuals change.
senses.whyCN: 这一社会义项把工程意象扩展到制度：规则像梁一样不均匀地分配优势，因此即使个人更替，模式仍然持续。

senses.title: Damage to the load-bearing frame
senses.definition: describing physical damage that affects the frame or foundation of a building, vehicle or machine rather than its surface
senses.definitionCN: 指影响建筑、车辆或机器框架或基础的物理损伤，而不是表面损伤
senses.example: The earthquake caused structural damage but no injuries.
senses.exampleCN: 地震造成了结构损伤，但无人受伤。
senses.why: This sense returns to the literal core: cosmetic cracks can be repaired, but structural damage means the part that carries the load is compromised, so the whole is at risk.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项回到字面核心：表面裂缝可以修补，而结构损伤意味着承重部件受损，整体因而处于风险中。

intro.en: Structural is structure plus the adjective ending -al; structure comes from Latin structura 'a building, a fitting together', from struere 'to build, pile up'. The deeper root is reconstructed.
intro.cn: structural 是 structure 加形容词词尾 -al；structure 出自拉丁 structura「建筑、拼合」，源自 struere「建造、堆叠」。其更深词根为重构形式。

items.en: Latin struere meant 'to build, pile up, arrange', and its past participle structus supplied the notion of something already built. The deeper root is reconstructed as Indo-European *streu- 'to spread, pile up'.
items.cn: 拉丁 struere 意为「建造、堆叠、安排」，其过去分词 structus 提供「已建成之物」的概念。更深词根被重构为印欧语 *streu-「铺开、堆积」。

items.en: Structura named the act of building and the building itself, hence 'a fitting together, an arrangement'. It is the direct source of English structure.
items.cn: structura 指建造行为及建筑物本身，因而表示「拼合、安排」。它是英语 structure 的直接来源。

items.en: English borrowed structure in the fifteenth century, first for buildings and later for the arrangement of any organized whole.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 structure，最初指建筑物，后来指任何有组织整体的排列方式。

items.en: The adjective structural appears later, formed on structure with -al, and spread in engineering, biology and grammar in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 形容词 structural 出现较晚，由 structure 加 -al 构成，并在十九世纪扩展到工程、生物与语法领域。

items.en: Twentieth-century linguistics and anthropology made structural a key term for systems of relations, giving the word its abstract, systemic sense.
items.cn: 二十世纪的语言学与人类学使 structural 成为「关系系统」的关键术语，赋予该词抽象的、系统性的义项。

items.en: First-attestation uncertainty: the earliest English citation of structural is unknown. Reconstructed form: the Indo-European root of struere, *streu-, is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word, and its exact semantic range remains disputed.
items.cn: 首见年代存疑：structural 的英语最早书证年代不确定。重构形式：struere 的印欧语词根 *streu- 属重构，并非有记录的真实词形，其确切语义范围仍有争议。

note.en: The first group separates the structure family by part of speech and use; the second gives near-synonyms for being fundamental to a system.
note.cn: 第一组按词性与用法区分 structure 词族；第二组给出表示「属于系统根本」的近义词。

entries.definition: The arrangement itself, or the act of arranging. Structural is the adjective describing it.
entries.definitionCN: 指排列本身，或安排的动作；structural 是描述它的形容词。

entries.definition: Having a definite plan or pattern. Structured describes a thing that was organized; structural describes what belongs to the frame.
entries.definitionCN: 指具有明确计划或模式；structured 描述被组织好的事物，structural 描述属于框架的东西。

entries.definition: The school of thought that analyses systems of relations. Structural is the adjective; structuralism is the doctrine.
entries.definitionCN: 指分析关系系统的学派；structural 是形容词，structuralism 是学说。

entries.definition: The adverb answering 'in what respect?'. Structural modifies a noun; structurally modifies a verb or adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，回答「在哪方面」；structural 修饰名词，structurally 修饰动词或形容词。

entries.definition: Affecting the whole system rather than a part. It stresses spread through the system; structural stresses the framework that causes the spread.
entries.definitionCN: 指影响整个系统而非局部；systemic 强调贯穿系统，structural 强调造成这种贯穿的框架。

entries.definition: Relating to the art and design of buildings. Structural concerns whether they stand; architectural concerns how they are conceived.
entries.definitionCN: 指建筑艺术与设计；structural 关心建筑能否站住，architectural 关心如何构思。

entries.definition: Relating to the way a group is arranged. It is the social counterpart of structural, which can also describe beams and molecules.
entries.definitionCN: 指群体的安排方式，是 structural 在社会领域的对应词，而 structural 也能描述梁柱与分子。

entries.definition: Serving as the base or basis. It points to what everything rests on, while structural points to how the parts are connected.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为基础或依据，强调一切所依托之物；structural 强调部分如何连接。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: structure + -al: of the frame that holds the parts together.
normal.cn: structure + -al：属于把各部分撑在一起的框架。

normal.en: The family runs structure, structured, structuralism, structuralist, restructure, infrastructure.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 structure、structured、structuralism、structuralist、restructure、infrastructure。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the range: structural damage, structural reform, structural adjustment, structural engineer.
normal.cn: 固定搭配展示范围：结构损伤、结构性改革、结构调整、结构工程师。

normal.en: A structure carries load; a structural problem is one in the load-bearing part.
normal.cn: 结构承担荷载；结构性问题就出在承重部分。

normal.en: Structural causes outlast individual choices.
normal.cn: 结构性原因比个人选择更持久。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge cut open so the beams and the arrows of load are visible.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥被剖开，梁柱与荷载箭头都可见。

abstract.en: Picture a building whose walls are rules rather than bricks.
abstract.cn: 想象一座建筑，墙体是规则而不是砖块。

abstract.en: Picture a skeleton inside a body, holding up everything that looks soft.
abstract.cn: 想象身体里的一副骨架，撑起所有看似柔软的部分。

examples.en: The inspection found structural cracks in three of the columns.
examples.cn: 检查发现其中三根柱子有结构裂缝。

examples.en: High youth unemployment is a structural problem, not a seasonal one.
examples.cn: 青年高失业率是结构性问题，而不是季节性问题。

examples.en: Structural biology maps the shape of proteins to explain their function.
examples.cn: 结构生物学绘制蛋白质的形状，以解释其功能。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「structure（结构）+ al」——看骨架，不看表皮 → structural 结构的

root: 拉丁 struere「建造、堆叠」→ 过去分词 structus → 拉丁 structura「建筑、拼合」→ 英语 structure + -al。更深词根为重构形式 *streu-。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from arrangement in general to load-bearing frames, language systems, underlying causes, framework-changing reform, molecular shape, social inequality and literal structural damage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一般排列方式，扩展到承重框架、语言系统、深层原因、改变框架的改革、分子形态、社会不平等，最后回到字面上的结构损伤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a visible frame carries weight from the top down to the base.
core.cn: 核心意象：可见的框架把重量从顶部一路传到基座。

branches.en: ARRANGEMENT AS SUCH: how the parts are put together to make a whole.
branches.cn: 排列本身：各部分如何拼合成一个整体。

branches.en: LOAD PATH: beams and foundations carry weight, and damage there endangers the whole.
branches.cn: 荷载路径：梁与基础承担重量，此处受损会危及整体。

branches.en: SYSTEMS OF RELATIONS: sounds in a language, atoms in a molecule, arranged so that form explains function.
branches.cn: 关系系统：语言中的音、分子中的原子，其排列使形式解释功能。

branches.en: CAUSES BUILT INTO INSTITUTIONS: outcomes reproduced by rules rather than by individual choice.
branches.cn: 制度内置的原因：结果由规则而非个人选择不断再生产。

branches.en: REFORM AT THE FRAME: change the rules that generate outcomes, not just the outcomes.
branches.cn: 框架层面的改革：改变产生结果的规则，而不只是结果。

intro.en: Structural is a Latin-derived base plus an adjective ending: struere 'to build' gives structura, English structure, and then structural with -al.
intro.cn: structural 是拉丁词基加形容词词尾：struere「建造」给出 structura，英语作 structure，再加 -al 成为 structural。

latinIntro.en: Latin struere and structura also underlie construct, destruction, instruct, obstruct and infrastructure, all built on the image of piling parts into a frame.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 struere 与 structura 也支撑 construct、destruction、instruct、obstruct、infrastructure，都建立在「把部件堆成框架」的意象上。

items.example: The building has structural problems in the east wing.
items.exampleCN: 这座建筑东翼存在结构问题。

items.example: The structure of the argument is easy to follow.
items.exampleCN: 这一论证的结构很容易跟随。

items.example: The two buildings are structurally similar.
items.exampleCN: 这两座建筑在结构上相似。

items.example: Structuralism treated language as a system of differences.
items.exampleCN: 结构主义把语言视为差异系统。

items.meaningCN: 结构主义者；结构主义的
items.example: The structuralist read the myth as a pattern of oppositions.
items.exampleCN: 这位结构主义者把神话读成对立模式。

items.meaning: to organize again in a new way
items.example: The firm restructured its debt last year.
items.exampleCN: 该公司去年重组了债务。

items.meaning: the underlying systems a society needs
items.meaningCN: 社会所依赖的基础系统
items.example: Roads and water pipes are infrastructure.
items.exampleCN: 道路与水管属于基础设施。

items.meaning: the supporting part beneath a building
items.meaningCN: 建筑物下方的支撑部分
items.example: The substructure was reinforced with steel piles.

definition_zh: 根系；根系统；根的网络结构
definition_en: the entire network of roots belonging to a plant, including its main roots and all lateral branches
core_image: 草皮被切开后，草茎下方露出一张向四周均匀铺开的细密根网
scene: 研究人员挖开表土后发现，草地下方的根系像一张细密的网，向四周均匀铺开。 After the researchers removed the topsoil, they found a fine, even mesh of roots beneath the grass: a classic fibrous root system.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「须根系」（第 3 个义项：由大量细根构成的根系类型）；句意为研究者挖开表土后，发现草地下方是一张细密均匀的根网，即典型的须根系。

pos.zh: 根系；一株植物的全部根
（数学）根系统（李代数分类用的根向量集合）

senses.title: Whole root network
senses.definition: all the roots of a plant considered together as one network
senses.definitionCN: 把一株植物的所有根当作一个网络来看
senses.example: A mature oak may have a root system wider than its crown.
senses.exampleCN: 一棵成年橡树的根系可能比它的树冠还宽。
senses.why: The compound names the whole rather than any single root: the object is the network, not the organ.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词命名的是整体而非单条根：对象是网，而不是某个器官。

senses.title: Taproot system
senses.definition: a root system dominated by one main root that grows straight down, with smaller lateral roots branching from it
senses.definitionCN: 由一条向下直长的主根主导、侧根从其上分出的根系
senses.example: Carrots and dandelions develop a taproot system with one dominant root.
senses.exampleCN: 胡萝卜和蒲公英形成一条主根占主导的直根系。
senses.why: The type is defined by the dominance of the first root, which stays central while later roots stay subordinate.
senses.whyCN: 这一类型由第一条根的主导地位定义：主根居中，后来的根处于从属位置。

senses.title: Fibrous root system
senses.definition: a root system made of many roots of similar size, with no single dominant root
senses.definitionCN: 由许多粗细相近的根构成、没有单条主导根的根系
senses.example: Grasses spread a dense fibrous root system that binds the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 禾草铺开密集的须根系，把土壤固定住。
senses.why: Here the network is flat and even: no root wins, and the mass of fine roots does the work.
senses.whyCN: 这里网络扁平而均匀：没有哪条根占优，靠大量细根发挥作用。

senses.title: Lateral root spread
senses.definition: the outward spread of lateral roots that gives a root system its width
senses.definitionCN: 侧根向外伸展，使根系获得宽度
senses.example: Lateral roots extend outward and give the root system its spread.
senses.exampleCN: 侧根向外伸展，使根系铺展开来。
senses.why: Width comes from branching, so the same system can be read as a branching structure rather than a list of organs.
senses.whyCN: 宽度来自分枝，因此同一系统也可以读成一个分枝结构，而不是一串器官。

senses.title: Anchorage function
senses.definition: the function by which a root system holds a plant upright and resists being pulled out
senses.definitionCN: 根系把植物固定直立、抵抗拔出的功能
senses.example: The root system holds the tree upright during storms.
senses.exampleCN: 根系在风暴中把树固定住，使其保持直立。
senses.why: This sense names what the network does rather than what it is: the system is treated as an anchoring device.
senses.whyCN: 这一义命名网络的作用而非其构造：系统被当作一种锚固装置。

senses.title: Absorption and transport
senses.definition: the function by which a root system takes up water and dissolved nutrients and passes them to the shoot
senses.definitionCN: 根系吸收水分与溶解养分并向上输送的功能
senses.example: A shallow root system limits how much water the plant can reach.
senses.exampleCN: 浅根系限制了植株能够获取的水量。
senses.why: The network is now a plumbing and intake surface, which is why depth and fineness matter.
senses.whyCN: 这时网络是取水与输水的表面，因此深度与细度都很重要。

senses.title: Root system in mathematics
senses.definition: a finite set of vectors in Euclidean space, closed under reflection, used to classify semisimple Lie algebras
senses.definitionCN: 欧氏空间中在反射下封闭的有限向量集合，用于分类半单李代数
senses.example: The classification of Lie algebras depends on the root system attached to each one.
senses.exampleCN: 李代数的分类取决于附属于每一个李代数的根系统。
senses.why: This is a separate technical coinage: the vectors are called roots because they generate the structure, not because they resemble plant roots.
senses.whyCN: 这是独立的技术造词：这些向量被称为根，是因为它们生成整个结构，而不是因为像植物根。

senses.title: Foundational network (figurative)
senses.definition: the underlying network of groups or institutions that supports a larger movement
senses.definitionCN: 支撑一个更大运动的基层组织或机构网络
senses.example: The reform movement grew out of a root system of local clubs and unions.
senses.exampleCN: 这场改革运动从地方俱乐部与工会构成的基层网络中生长出来。
senses.why: The plant image is applied to society: many small units feed one visible structure above ground.
senses.whyCN: 植物意象被用于社会：许多小单元向上供养一个可见结构。

intro.en: The compound is transparent: a Germanic root word plus a Greek-derived system word. The botanical types are nineteenth-century, and the mathematical term has a separate history.
intro.cn: 复合词的构成清楚：前一词为日耳曼来源，后一词经拉丁语上溯希腊语。植物学两类型术语定型于十九世纪；数学义另有独立来源。

items.en: The first element is Old English rōt, reinforced by Old Norse rót, from Proto-Germanic *wrōts. It names the underground organ of a plant.
items.cn: 第一个成分是古英语 rōt，受古诺斯语 rót 强化，来自原始日耳曼语 *wrōts，指植物的地下器官。

items.en: The second element goes back to Greek systema 'an organized whole', through Late Latin systema. It contributes the idea of parts arranged as one working body.
items.cn: 第二个成分经晚期拉丁语 systema 上溯希腊语 systema「有组织的整体」，带来「各部分排成一个运作整体」的意思。

items.en: The compound root system is recorded in botanical writing, where it named all the roots of one plant taken together.
items.cn: 复合词 root system 见于植物学写作，用来指一株植物全部根的总和。

items.en: The taproot and fibrous types were distinguished as the two basic architectures of flowering plants, and the terms entered textbooks.
items.cn: 直根型与须根型被区分为被子植物的两种基本构型，相关术语进入教科书。

items.en: The mathematical root system arose independently in the theory of Lie algebras. Its 'roots' are generating vectors, not plant organs.
items.cn: 数学上的根系统在李代数理论中独立产生。其中的「根」是生成向量，不是植物器官。

items.en: The figurative use for organizational networks is a twentieth-century extension, common in writing about social movements.
items.cn: 用于组织网络的比喻义是二十世纪延伸，常见于社会运动写作。

note.en: Two groups follow: the first is close in sound or form and easy to mix up; the second shares part of the meaning but is not interchangeable.
note.cn: 分两组：第一组在读音或形式上接近、容易混淆；第二组只共享部分意思，不能互换。

entries.definition: a single tiny tubular outgrowth of a root, not the whole network; it is one thread, not a system.
entries.definitionCN: 根毛。根表面单条微小的管状突起，不是整个网络；它是一根丝，不是一个系统。

entries.definition: the stem, leaves and flowers above ground; it is the upward counterpart of the root system.
entries.definitionCN: 茎叶系统。地上的茎、叶与花，是根系向上的对应系统。

entries.definition: the root and lower stem of a plant, often used for grafting; it is one part, not the full network.
entries.definitionCN: 根砧；根茎。植物的根与下部茎，常用于嫁接；是单个部位，不是完整网络。

entries.definition: a plain descriptive phrase for connected roots; it stresses connection but does not name a botanical type.
entries.definitionCN: 根网络。平实的描述性短语，强调连接，但不命名植物学类型。

entries.definition: the spatial arrangement of a root system, including depth, spread and branching; it describes the shape rather than the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 根系构型。根系的空间排列，包括深度、展幅与分枝；描述形状而非整体。

entries.definition: the one dominant root of a taproot system; the system contains it, but it is not the system.
entries.definitionCN: 主根；直根。直根系中那条占主导的根；系统包含它，但它不等于系统。

entries.definition: the many fine roots of a fibrous system; the phrase names the roots, while root system names their arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 须根。须根系中大量细根；该短语命名根本身，而 root system 命名它们的排列。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The compound is literal: the roots of one plant plus the system they form.
normal.cn: 这个复合词是字面组合：一株植物的根，加上它们构成的系统。

normal.en: Botany contrasts two basic types: taproot system and fibrous root system.
normal.cn: 植物学对比两种基本类型：直根系与须根系。

normal.en: The functional words are anchorage and absorption, which is why depth matters.
normal.cn: 功能关键词是固着与吸收，这正是深度重要的原因。

normal.en: Root architecture and lateral root are the usual companions in research writing.
normal.cn: 根系构型与侧根是研究写作中的常见配套词。

normal.en: The mathematical sense belongs to Lie algebra, not to botany.
normal.cn: 数学义属于李代数，与植物学无关。

abstract.en: Picture a grass sod lifted like a carpet, the underside a dense even mat.
abstract.cn: 想象一块草皮像地毯一样被掀起，背面是一张密集均匀的垫子。

abstract.en: Picture a carrot pulled from the soil, one long root with small side threads.
abstract.cn: 想象一根胡萝卜被拔出，一条长主根带着细小的侧根。

abstract.en: Picture an organization chart drawn as roots feeding a single trunk above ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一张组织图被画成根在地下供养地上的一根主干。

examples.en: The seedlings were planted with their root systems kept moist.
examples.cn: 幼苗栽下时，根系保持湿润。

examples.en: A deep root system lets the shrub survive a long dry season.
examples.cn: 深根系让这种灌木熬过漫长的旱季。

examples.en: Engineers study root system architecture to stabilize slopes.
examples.cn: 工程人员研究根系构型，用来稳固坡面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「根 + 系统」——一株植物所有根连成的一整套网络 → 根系

root: 前一词为古英语 rōt / 古诺斯语 rót，来自原始日耳曼语 *wrōts；后一词经晚期拉丁语 systema 上溯希腊语 systema「有组织的整体」。植物学两类型术语定型于十九世纪，数学义为独立造词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move between whole and type, structure and function, and finally between botany, mathematics and society. The same compound can name a plant's entire underground body, one of its two basic architectures, a spatial pattern, a job, a set of vectors or a social base.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项在整体与类型、结构与功能之间移动，最后跨越植物学、数学与社会。同一个复合词可以指一株植物的全部地下身体、两种基本构型之一、一种空间格局、一项功能、一组向量或一个社会基础。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an underground mat wider than the plant above it, every thread connected.
core.cn: 核心意象：地下一张比地上植株更宽的网络，每一根丝都相连。

branches.en: WHOLE AND SPREAD: the network as a whole, and the laterals that give it width.
branches.cn: 整体与展幅：作为整体的网络，以及赋予它宽度的侧根。

branches.en: TWO ARCHITECTURES: one dominant root or many equal roots.
branches.cn: 两种构型：一条主导根，或许多等大的根。

branches.en: FUNCTIONS: the same network either anchors or feeds.
branches.cn: 功能：同一网络，或用于固定，或用于供养。

branches.en: MATHEMATICAL GENERATION: vectors that generate a structure are called roots by analogy.
branches.cn: 数学生成：生成结构的向量被类比称为根。

branches.en: SOCIAL BASE: many small units support one visible structure.
branches.cn: 社会基础：许多小单元支撑一个可见结构。

intro.en: The compound joins a Germanic root word to a Greek-derived system word, so its two halves come from different layers of English vocabulary.
intro.cn: 这个复合词把日耳曼来源的根词与希腊来源的系统词接在一起，两半来自英语词汇的不同层次。

latinIntro.en: Latin radix is a cognate of root and supplies the technical term; Greek systema reached English through Late Latin systema. Neither half is a direct Latin derivative of the compound.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 radix 是 root 的同源词并提供技术术语；希腊语 systema 经晚期拉丁语 systema 进入英语。两半都不是这个复合词的直接拉丁派生。

definition_zh: n. 性情；倾向；处置；部署
definition_en: the natural qualities of a person character, or the way things are arranged or dealt with
core_image: 吵闹房间里依旧平和的一张脸；遗嘱上被分成几堆并贴好标签的财物；作战地图上被移动的小旗

senses.title: Natural character
senses.definition: the natural qualities of a person character
senses.definitionCN: （名词）一个人性格中天生的那些特质
senses.example: She has a cheerful disposition.
senses.exampleCN: 她性情愉快。
senses.why: A calm face that stays calm in a noisy room.
senses.whyCN: 在吵闹房间里依旧平和的一张脸。

senses.title: Dealing with property
senses.definition: the way something is arranged, sold or given away
senses.definitionCN: （名词）某物被安排、出售或分配的方式
senses.example: The will sets out the disposition of the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 遗嘱写明了遗产的处置方式。
senses.why: A table of items being sorted into labelled piles.
senses.whyCN: 一桌东西被分进贴好标签的几堆。

senses.title: Arrangement of forces
senses.definition: the arrangement of troops or resources in position
senses.definitionCN: （名词）部队或资源在位置上的排布

senses.exampleCN: 将军研究了自己兵力的部署。
senses.why: Small flags moved across a map before a battle.
senses.whyCN: 战前在地图上被移动的小旗。

senses.title: A tendency

senses.exampleCN: 他有夸大其词的倾向。
senses.why: A hand that keeps adding one more fish to the story.
senses.whyCN: 一只不停往故事里再加一条鱼的手。

intro.en: Disposition comes from Latin dispositio, arrangement, from disponere, to set in order, itself from dis- plus ponere, to put; the sense of inner character grows out of the idea of how things are arranged inside a person.
intro.cn: disposition 来自拉丁语 dispositio「布置」，源自 disponere「安排整齐」，后者由 dis- 加 ponere「放置」组成；「性情」义正是从「一个人内部如何排布」这个想法长出来的。

items.en: Latin ponere means to put or place.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ponere 意为放置。

items.en: Disponere meant to arrange or set in order.
items.cn: disponere 意为安排、布置整齐。

items.en: Dispositio meant an arrangement or ordering.

items.en: Old French disposition keeps the sense of arrangement.
items.cn: 古法语 disposition 保留布置的意思。

items.en: English disposition extends to a person natural temper.
items.cn: 英语 disposition 扩展到人天生的脾气。

items.en: The word is used for the placing of troops.
items.cn: 这个词被用于部队的布置。

note.en: Disposition is how things are put in order, inside a person or on a map; its look-alikes share the put root and its neighbours name character and layout.
note.cn: disposition 是事物被排布的方式，无论在人心里还是在地图上；形近词共用放置词根，近义词则指性格与布局。

senses.title: Food and nourishment

senses.example: Bread and salt were the poor man's aliment.
senses.exampleCN: 面包和盐是穷人的口粮。

senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 alimentum 意为「给养」：凡喂进去而维持生命者皆为 aliment。

senses.title: Legal support for a dependent
senses.definition: the legal obligation, or the money paid, to support a relative who cannot support themselves

senses.example: The decree fixed the amount of aliment at forty pounds a month.

senses.why: If nourishment keeps a body alive, the law transfers the same duty to relatives: support is owed like food is owed.
senses.whyCN: 滋养维系生命，法律便把这同一义务转给亲属：扶养如食物一样是应尽之责。

senses.title: To nourish or sustain
senses.definition: to provide food or support to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 向某人或某物提供食物或支持
senses.example: Hope alimented the settlers through the first winter.
senses.exampleCN: 希望支撑着移民们熬过第一个冬天。
senses.why: The noun passes into a verb: to give aliment is to aliment.
senses.whyCN: 名词转作动词：给予给养（aliment）这一动作即 aliment。

intro.en: From a Latin verb of feeding, carrying its sense of nourishment into law and biology.
intro.cn: 来自一个拉丁语的「喂养」动词，把「滋养」之义带进法律与生物学。

items.en: A reconstructed root *al- meant to grow or nourish, also behind old, adult, and altitude.
items.cn: 重构词根 *al- 意为生长、滋养，也是 old、adult、altitude 的来源。

items.en: alere meant to feed and nourish; alimentum meant sustenance.
items.cn: 拉丁语 alere 意为喂养、滋养；alimentum 意为给养。

items.en: In legal Latin, alimentum named the duty to support a dependent relative.
items.cn: 中世纪法律拉丁语中，alimentum 指供养亲属的义务。

items.en: English took aliment in both senses, food and legal support, and later as a verb.
items.cn: 16 世纪英语兼收两义——食物与法律扶养，后又用作动词。

items.en: The noun is now rare outside Scottish law and scientific compounds; its descendants alimentary and alimony are common.
items.cn: 现代英语中该名词除苏格兰法与科学复合词外已少用；其后代 alimentary 与 alimony 更常见。

note.en: The first group gathers the nourishing family and a spelling twin; the second gathers words for sustenance.
note.cn: 第一组收滋养词族与一个形近词；第二组收表示「给养」的词。

normalIntro.en: From Latin alere, to feed: what is fed in keeps life going.
normalIntro.cn: 来自拉丁语 alere「喂养」：喂进去的东西维持着生命。

normal.en: alimentary canal is the everyday descendant: the digestive tract.
normal.cn: alimentary canal 是它最常见的后代：消化道。

normal.en: In Scottish law, aliment is child support.
normal.cn: 在苏格兰法中，aliment 指子女抚养费。

normal.en: alimony is its cousin: money for a former spouse.
normal.cn: alimony 是它的近亲：离婚生活费。

normal.en: The root *al- also gives old and adult: growth.
normal.cn: 词根 *al- 也派生 old 与 adult：都与「长」有关。

normal.en: Figuratively, news can be the mind's aliment.
normal.cn: 比喻用法中，消息可以是精神食粮。

abstract.en: Picture bread and salt set before a hungry labourer.
abstract.cn: 想象面包和盐摆在饥饿的劳工面前。

abstract.en: See a coin passed each month from one hand to an older one.
abstract.cn: 想象每月一枚硬币从一只手递向一双更苍老的手。

abstract.en: Imagine hope as thin soup that still keeps a man on his feet.
abstract.cn: 想象希望是一碗稀汤，却仍撑着一个人站立。

examples.en: The parish was bound to provide aliment for the orphans.
examples.cn: 教区有义务供养这些孤儿。

examples.en: Ideas are the aliment of a curious mind.
examples.cn: 思想是好奇之心的精神食粮。

examples.en: She alimented the whole household on a weaver's wage.
examples.cn: 她靠织工的微薄工资养活全家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱立门特」——爱吃能立住门面的特长：先喂饱，才能站立。

root: 拉丁语 alere「喂养」派生 alimentum「给养」，更早可溯至重构词根 *al-「生长、滋养」（同源词 old、adult、altitude）；经中世纪法律拉丁语兼指「扶养义务」，16 世纪进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses follow one feeding pipe: the food itself, the legal duty to provide it, and the act of feeding.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项沿同一条「输送管道」展开：食物本身，供给食物的法律义务，以及喂养的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: bread passed hand to hand, keeping a life going one mouthful at a time.
core.cn: 核心意象：面包手手相传，一口一口把生命续下去。
